articles.title: It Still Needs More Time to Dry
articles.summary: Mia’s group has to print twelve posters before lunch. She cannot understand the teacher’s whole sentence, so at first she can only follow the wet ink, the drying rack, and the gesture well enough to keep the work moving.
articles.summaryZh: 米娅必须和同组在午饭前印完十二张海报。她听不懂老师的整句话，只能先跟着湿墨、晾架和手势把事情做对。
storyParagraphs: On Saturday morning, Mia attended a Dutch-language community screen-printing class for the first time. Her group had to finish twelve event posters before lunch. At 1:00 p.m., open-day staff would collect them to put up at the entrance and along the street; if wet ink was smudged by stacking, there would be no time to reprint. Mia understood colors, numbers, and words like “here” and “there,” but full sentences often left her with only a few familiar words. Just after the first poster was printed, she reached to stack two sheets. The teacher held up the top one, pointed to the black ink, and said, “Nog niet. De inkt moet nog drogen.” Then she placed the sheet on the drying rack.

Mia did not understand every word, but she understood that she should not do that yet. When the second sheet came out, she put it on the drying rack herself and went on helping the group pull the next print. The teacher said “moet nog drogen” again and this time only pointed to the timer. Ten minutes later, when the edges of the first batch were no longer shiny, the teacher said “nu wel,” and the three of them quickly moved the dry posters to the long table to free space on the rack for the rest.

After all twelve posters were finished on time, there was still a small wooden sign coated in blue paint that had to be prepared for the entrance table. Another student asked whether they could turn it over and write on the other side. The teacher touched the surface and said, “De verf moet nog drogen.” Mia first recognized the familiar “moet nog drogen,” then noticed that “verf” was different from the earlier “inkt.” On her ink-spotted note paper, she wrote: “inkt / verf — moet nog drogen”.

After lunch, staff came to collect the posters, and one test print was also slipped into a paper bag. Mia touched the edge and found it still slightly tacky. She said, “Nog niet… het moet nog drogen.” The teacher nodded; when there were three more sheets beside it, she added, “Ze moeten nog drogen.” The staff member heard this, put the paper bag back on the table, and carried away the stack that was already fully dry. Mia wrote the plural sentence beside the ink spots on her note paper.

The following week, the class switched to printing tote bags; none of the posters or the wooden sign from the first week were there. After the last screen was washed, someone in Mia’s group started folding the freshly printed bags into a box and asked, “Kunnen ze erin?” Mia blocked the lid and said, “Nog niet. Ze moeten nog drogen.” The teacher was putting away tools at another table and did not come over to demonstrate. Her classmate spread the bags back out on the rack.

Near the end of class, the open-day coordinator called from the hallway and asked whether a new set of direction signs in the drying room next door could be taken away now. Mia was standing by the sink and could not see the signs. She asked the teacher only, “Nu?” The teacher, still wearing her gloves, shook her head and said only, “Morgen.” Mia told the caller, “Nog niet. Ze moeten nog drogen.” The caller said they would come back the next morning. Mia put the phone back on its charging dock and turned to keep rinsing the squeegee.
storyParagraphsZh: 周六上午，米娅第一次参加荷兰语社区丝网印刷课，午饭前要和同组印完十二张活动海报。下午一点，开放日工作人员会来取海报贴入口和路口；湿墨一旦被叠花，就没有时间重印。米娅能听懂颜色、数字和“这里”“那里”，完整句子却常只剩几个熟词。第一张刚印完，她伸手想把两张纸叠起来，老师托住上面那张，指着黑墨说：“Nog niet. De inkt moet nog drogen.”又把纸送进晾架。
米娅没听懂每个词，却明白这一步不能做。第二张出来后，她自己把纸送进晾架，继续帮同组刮下一张。老师再次说“moet nog drogen”，这次只指了指计时器。十分钟后第一批纸边不再发亮，老师说“nu wel”，三个人赶紧把干的移到长桌，空出晾架给后面的海报。
十二张按时印完后，上午还剩一块涂过蓝漆的木牌要给入口桌用。另一个同学问能不能翻面写字，老师碰了碰表面，说：“De verf moet nog drogen.”米娅先听出熟悉的“moet nog drogen”，再注意到前面的“verf”和刚才的“inkt”不同。她在沾了墨点的笔记纸上写下：“inkt / verf — moet nog drogen”。
午饭后，工作人员来取海报，其中一张试印品也被顺手塞进纸袋。米娅摸到边角还有一点黏，说：“Nog niet… het moet nog drogen.”老师点头；旁边还有三张时，她补了一句：“Ze moeten nog drogen.”工作人员听见后把纸袋放回桌上，改先搬已经干透的那一叠。米娅把复数那句记在墨点旁边。
下一周课程换成印布袋，第一周的海报和木牌都没有带来。洗完最后一块网版时，同组的人准备把刚印好的布袋叠进箱子，有人问：“Kunnen ze erin?”米娅挡住箱盖，说：“Nog niet. Ze moeten nog drogen.”老师正在另一张桌收工具，没有过来示范；同伴直接把布袋重新摊到架子上。
快下课时，开放日负责人从走廊打来电话，问隔壁晾室的一批新指示牌现在能不能带走。米娅在水槽边看不见那些牌，只问老师一句：“Nu?”老师还戴着手套，只摇头说：“Morgen.”米娅对电话那头说：“Nog niet. Ze moeten nog drogen.”对方回答明早再来。她把电话放回充电座，转身继续冲洗刮板。
explanationParagraphs: Comprehensible input is language whose overall meaning a learner can grasp without knowing every word or form, because familiar language, objects, actions, context, repetition, and interaction provide support. Krashen stressed understanding input that contains new forms, but “i+1” is not a precisely measurable formula.

Guessing one instruction from visible objects is not the same as building a reusable pattern. The story repeats one clause across materials and tasks while Mia distinguishes singular and plural forms. Input matters, but output, interaction, feedback, attention, and participation also shape development; one course does not equal complete acquisition.
explanationParagraphsZh: 可理解输入是学习者尚未掌握全部词汇或语法，却能借助已知语言、实物、动作、情境、重复和互动把握整体意义的材料。Krashen 强调理解含有新形式的输入对习得的重要性，但“i+1”不是可精确测量的公式。
借现场物件猜懂一次指令，不等于形成可复用的语言结构。故事让同一主句跨材料和任务重现，并让米娅区分单数与复数表达。输入很重要，输出、互动、反馈、注意和参与也会影响发展；一次课程不能代表完整习得。
articles.overallZh: 第一次送纸进晾架主要证明米娅借助湿墨、动作和共同任务理解了事件意义。之后同一主句结构在油墨、油漆、布袋和不在眼前的指示牌上重复出现，她才开始注意并复用单复数形式。结尾电话改变了对方的取件安排，但仍只支持“开始建立这个形式”，不证明稳定掌握。
articles.overall: Putting the first wet poster on the drying rack mainly shows that Mia could understand the event through the ink, the teacher’s action, and the shared task. Only after the same main-clause structure reappears with ink, paint, tote bags, and direction signs that are not in front of her does she begin to notice and reuse the singular and plural forms. The final phone call changes the pickup plan, but it supports only that she is beginning to build and reuse the form, not that her use of it is already stable.

moduleZh.intro: 海报必须在午饭前完成，所以米娅首先需要的是把工作做对。湿墨、动作和晾架让一句含有新形式的话可以被理解；同一结构后来跨过不同材料和任务反复出现，她才开始自己选用单数和复数形式。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 可理解输入如何从情境支持走向开始复用语言形式
diagramSteps: 实物、动作和共同任务先让整体意义可以被理解
同一主句结构在真实任务中重复出现
更换材料和名词，使意义不只绑定最初道具
学习者开始尝试单数与复数形式并获得自然回应
原物不在眼前时，学习者仍自行选择形式完成沟通
diagramStepNotes: 第一次听到“De inkt moet nog drogen”时，湿墨、托纸动作和晾架承担了大量意义支持，因此不能单凭正确行动断言形式已被习得。
“De verf moet nog drogen”保留同一主句语序，却更换名词与材料，使熟悉结构跨出第一张海报。
“het moet nog drogen”和“ze moeten nog drogen”分别是自然的单数、复数主句形式；故事不把嵌入从句的不同词序混作同一个目标结构。
第五段米娅在新材料布袋上主动使用复数形式，已经比单纯跟随动作更接近复用，但仍不足以证明稳定掌握。
电话结尾老师只摇头并说已知时间词“Morgen”，米娅自己选择“Ze moeten nog drogen”，对方据此改到明早取件，带来新的实际行动结果。
mapping: 湿墨、托住纸张与晾架 → 非语言和共同情境先支撑整体意义。
油漆木牌再次出现相同主句结构 → 新形式在改变材料后仍可被追踪。
单张试印品用“het”，多张用“ze” → 学习者开始把形式与数量关系连接。
第二周对布袋主动说“Ze moeten nog drogen” → 原海报道具不在场时开始复用。
电话里看不见指示牌仍自行使用复数结构 → 语言形式开始在更少现场支撑下承担可行动的意义。
moduleZh.boundary: 可理解输入不是逐词翻译，也不是把语言降低到零新意；“i+1”更适合作为方向性概念，而不是可精确计算的教学公式。一次根据情境做对动作不能自动证明习得，输入也不是唯一充分条件。本故事只显示米娅开始建立并复用一个目标形式，不证明一次课程完成稳定习得。课程、人物与事件均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么第一次看着湿墨把纸送进晾架，只能说明米娅理解了事情，而电话里看不见指示牌仍能自行说出“Ze moeten nog drogen”，提供的是不同层次的证据？

module.intro: The posters must be finished before lunch, so Mia first needs to keep the work moving correctly. Wet ink, gestures, and the drying rack make a sentence containing a new form understandable. Only after the structure returns across different materials and tasks does she begin choosing its singular and plural forms herself.
module.diagramTitle: How comprehensible input can move from contextual support toward beginning reuse of a language form
diagramSteps: Objects, actions, and the shared task first make the overall meaning understandable
The same new main-clause structure recurs during a real task
Materials and nouns change so the meaning is no longer tied to the first object
The learner begins trying singular and plural forms and receives natural responses
With the original object out of sight, the learner still chooses the form independently to complete communication
diagramStepNotes: When Mia first hears “De inkt moet nog drogen,” the wet ink, the teacher holding the sheet, and the drying rack provide much of the meaning, so correct action alone cannot establish that the form has been acquired.
“De verf moet nog drogen” keeps the same main-clause word order while changing the noun and material, carrying the familiar structure beyond the first poster.

“het moet nog drogen” and “ze moeten nog drogen” are natural singular and plural main-clause forms; the story does not treat the different word order of an embedded clause as the same target structure.

In the fifth paragraph, Mia independently uses the plural form with a new material, the tote bags. This is stronger evidence of reuse than simply following an action, but it still does not show stable control of the form.

In the final phone call, the teacher only shakes her head and says the familiar time word “Morgen.” Mia chooses “Ze moeten nog drogen” herself, and the caller changes the pickup to the next morning, producing a new practical consequence.
mapping: Wet ink, the held sheet, and the drying rack → nonverbal information and shared context first support overall meaning.
The painted wooden sign brings back the same main-clause structure → the new form remains traceable after the material changes.
One test print takes “het,” several sheets take “ze” → the learner begins connecting the form with singular and plural reference.
Mia independently says “Ze moeten nog drogen” about tote bags in the second week → she begins reusing the expression without the original poster context.
On the phone, she cannot see the direction signs but still chooses the plural structure herself → the language form begins carrying actionable meaning with less immediate visual support.
module.boundary: Comprehensible input is not word-for-word translation and does not require reducing language to zero novelty; “i+1” is better treated as a directional idea than as an exactly calculable teaching formula. Acting correctly once from context does not automatically prove acquisition, and input is not the only sufficient condition. This story shows only that Mia is beginning to build and reuse one target form; it does not show that her use has become stable after one course. The class, characters, and events are fictional.
module.reflection: Why does putting the first wet poster on the rack mainly show that Mia understood the situation, while independently saying “Ze moeten nog drogen” about unseen signs over the phone provides a different kind of evidence?

articles.title: The Third Past Tense in the Handover Log
articles.titleZh: 交班本上的第三种过去时
articles.summary: Before the end-of-month schedule is fixed, Zhou Ran’s formal handovers look increasingly correct, yet her supervisor still cannot see what English she can produce herself. A few preserved drafts begin to reveal another, changing pattern.
articles.summaryZh: 月底排班前，周然的正式交班越来越正确，主管却仍看不出她本人在使用怎样的英语。几张被保留下来的原稿，开始讲出另一条变化中的线索。
storyParagraphs: Zhou Ran had just started working night shifts at the youth-hostel front desk, and the end-of-month schedule already contained two possible nights when she might work independently. Morning staff needed the handover log to continue dealing with broken keys, maintenance issues, and outstanding charges, so supervisor Emma could not leave unclear notes as they were. In the first week Zhou Ran often wrote: “Guest call at 11. I give new key. He go back room.” Each night Emma first rewrote it into a clear standard version so the morning shift could work from the formal log.

By the second week, Emma realized that the clean formal log alone did not tell her whether Zhou Ran could really be trusted with an independent night shift by the end of the month. She still made sure the morning staff received a clear corrected version, but she began attaching Zhou Ran’s original page behind each day’s handover and writing the date on it. Across several nights, completed events repeatedly appeared as call, give, go, and buy; even when the sentence already contained last night or yesterday, the verbs often remained in the bare form. Emma marked corrections beside only a few high-frequency verbs while the actual front-desk work continued as usual.

On Friday night, the guest in Room 214 called twice because the key card had stopped working. After handling it, Zhou Ran wrote: “Guest called twice. I checked old card. He goed upstairs.” That same night another group bought two breakfast tickets, and she wrote: “They buyed two breakfast tickets.” The next morning, staff used the handover to continue checking the door lock and the ticket numbers. Emma corrected the formal page to went and bought, but kept the original page containing called, checked, goed, and buyed attached behind it.

On the next, quieter night, Zhou Ran prepared her handover summary ten minutes before the shift ended. She wrote “Guest went upstairs” and “They bought breakfast tickets,” and in new events she wrote “Room 108 opened late” and “I called maintenance.” Near the end of the shift, a morning colleague unexpectedly phoned early to ask where the Room 214 guest was now. Without looking at the log, Zhou Ran said aloud: “He go upstairs, then call me.” After the call, she wrote the time and that sentence on a sticky note and clipped it into that day’s handover page.

Before the end of the month, the front-desk manager had to decide whether the two independent night shifts should remain on Zhou Ran’s schedule. Besides reviewing the original language samples, the manager checked whether key numbers had been mixed up, whether the Room 214 repair had actually been handed over to the morning team, and whether the cash and breakfast tickets reconciled. The work itself could be taken over successfully, although Zhou Ran’s spoken and written English still did not always look the same. The manager kept the two independent nights, with an experienced colleague available by phone overnight during the first week; Zhou Ran was still required to review the formal handover herself before ending each shift.

On the final training night, Zhou Ran finished the formal handover. The top line read: “Guest went out at 10 and came back at 11:30.” She put a copy in the transparent folder. Beside the opening was still the sticky note: “he go upstairs, then call me — 06:42.” Under the folder lay the new schedule, with her name already entered in the two night-shift boxes.
storyParagraphsZh: 周然刚到青年旅舍前台上夜班，月底排班表已经给她留了两个可能独立值班的夜晚。白班早上要靠交班本继续处理坏钥匙、维修和未结费用，所以主管艾玛不能把含糊记录直接留下。第一周周然常写：“Guest call at 11. I give new key. He go back room.”艾玛每晚先改成清楚的标准版本，再让白班照正式本接手。
到了第二周，艾玛发现只看正式本没法判断月底能不能真的把夜班交给周然。她仍保证白班拿到修改后的清楚版本，但开始把周然原稿订在当天交班页后面，写上日期。连续几晚，已经发生的事情反复出现call、give、go、buy；即使句子里已有last night、yesterday，动词也常保持原形。艾玛只在几个高频词旁做纠正记号，工作本身照常继续。

周五夜里，214房客两次打电话说门卡失效。周然处理完后写：“Guest called twice. I checked old card. He goed upstairs.”同一晚另一组客人买了两张早餐券，她又写：“They buyed two breakfast tickets.”白班第二天根据记录继续检查门锁和券号；艾玛在正式页里改成went和bought，但把带有called、checked、goed、buyed的原稿仍订在后面。

下一次夜班较安静，周然在交班前十分钟自己整理摘要，写出“Guest went upstairs”“They bought breakfast tickets”，还在新的事件里写了“Room 108 opened late”“I called maintenance”。临近下班，白班同事突然提前打电话追问214房客的位置。周然没有看本子，口头说：“He go upstairs, then call me.”电话结束后，她把时间和这句话写在一张便签上，夹进当天交班页。
月底前，前台经理要决定那两个独立夜班是否保留。他除了看这些原稿，也核对了钥匙编号有没有交错、214房维修是否真的转给白班、现金和早餐券是否对得上。工作内容都能继续接手，但口头和书面英语仍不完全一样。经理保留两个独立夜班，第一周安排资深同事凌晨可电话支援；正式交班仍要求周然下班前自己复查。
最后一个培训夜，周然写完正式交班。最上面一行是：“Guest went out at 10 and came back at 11:30.”她把副本放进透明袋。袋口旁还夹着那张便签：“he go upstairs, then call me — 06:42。”新排班表压在袋下，两个夜班格里已经写上她的名字。
explanationParagraphs: Interlanguage is the dynamic but systematic language system learners form while moving toward a target language. Prior languages, target-language input, learner-inferred rules, feedback, and communication strategies can all shape it. Errors may reflect a rule currently in use rather than random carelessness; as an older pattern recedes, a new regularized overgeneralization may appear.

Interlanguage also varies with task, preparation, attention, time pressure, and spoken or written conditions. The story does not assign the phone-call return to bare forms to one cause; it treats the difference as contextual variation. Developmental patterns require samples across time and tasks, and supervisor feedback remains part of the learning process.
explanationParagraphsZh: 中介语是学习者走向目标语时形成的动态而有系统的语言系统。它会受到既有语言、目标语输入、学习者自行推导的规则、反馈与沟通策略影响。错误可能反映当时正在使用的规则，而非随机粗心；旧模式减少时，也可能出现新的规则化过度概括。
中介语也会随任务、准备程度、注意分配、时间压力及口语或书写条件而变化。故事没有把电话里的原形回返归因于单一条件，只把差异作为情境变异来观察。判断发展模式需要跨时间、跨任务的多份样本，主管反馈也属于学习过程的一部分。
articles.overallZh: 保留原稿后，多个动词才显出可重复变化：早期原形持续出现，随后called、checked等规则过去时增多，同时出现goed、buyed等过度概括；后来went、bought和新的规则形式进入准备充分的书写，而临时电话仍会出现原形。样本支持一个正在变化的系统，但不能把书写／口语差异归因于单一压力因素。
articles.overall: Once the original pages are preserved, repeated change becomes visible across several verbs: early bare forms persist, then regular past forms such as called and checked increase while overgeneralizations such as goed and buyed also appear. Later, went and bought and new regular forms appear in more prepared writing, while the unplanned phone call still contains a bare form. The samples support a changing system, but the spoken/written difference cannot be attributed to time pressure alone.

moduleZh.intro: 正式交班页继续让白班能够工作，原稿则留下周然自己的表达。把多日、多动词和不同任务条件并排阅读，可以看见规则形式、过度概括和情境变化怎样在同一时期共存。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 中介语如何在多份真实产出中显出规则、重组与变异
diagramSteps: 先保留真实工作所需的清楚正式版本
同时保存学习者原始产出，跨日寻找重复模式
观察旧形式减少时是否出现新的规则化和过度概括
比较不同任务、准备程度与口语书写条件下的变化
把语言样本与实际工作表现一起用于谨慎的后续决定
diagramStepNotes: 第一周，多个动词在last night、yesterday等明确过去时间语境中仍反复使用原形，形成跨日期、跨词项的模式。
called、checked等规则形式与goed、buyed同时出现：新形成的过去时规则既产生目标形式，也被扩展到不规则动词。
went、bought进入准备充分的书写后，新的事件还出现opened、called。主管反馈参与了学习，而后续变化也出现在更多词项上。
临时电话与准备摘要同时改变了模态、准备时间、注意和时间压力，所以电话里的he go只显示情境变异，不能证明压力单独导致回返。
经理同时检查钥匙、维修、现金与券号是否正确交接。语言样本与实际工作结果共同决定支援安排和独立夜班。
mapping: 早期call、give、go、buy反复用于过去事件 → 跨动词重复减少单次粗心解释。
called、checked与goed、buyed并存 → 新规则进入后既产生目标形式也产生过度概括。
准备书写中的went、bought、opened、called → 后续产出不只复制两个被纠正答案。
电话中的he go与同夜书面过去时并存 → 同一时期的产出会随任务和模态条件变化。
正式交班、原稿、电话便签和实际交接结果一起保留 → 发展判断来自纵向多条件证据，而非单个正确句或单次回返。
moduleZh.boundary: 中介语不是两种语言的随机混合，也不是每次波动都代表进步。任务、准备、注意、压力、口语与书写等条件常同时变化，单个故事不能隔离它们各自的因果作用。反馈也可能参与学习。多份样本只能支持对当时系统性模式与变异的谨慎判断，不能凭一次表现诊断学习者的全部语言能力。旅舍、人物与语言样本均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么同一时期书面记录里的went、bought和电话里的he go需要一起保留，而不能只拿其中一类表现来判断周然‘已经会了’或‘又退步了’？

module.intro: The formal handover keeps the morning shift able to work, while the attached drafts preserve Zhou Ran’s own language. Reading several days, verbs, and task conditions together shows regular forms, overgeneralizations, and contextual variation coexisting at the same stage.
module.diagramTitle: How interlanguage shows rules, restructuring, and variation across real samples
diagramSteps: Keep a clear formal version for the real work
Also preserve the learner’s original output and look for repeated patterns across days
Observe whether new regularization and overgeneralization appear as older forms decrease
Compare changes across tasks, preparation levels, and spoken versus written conditions
Use language samples together with actual job performance for cautious later decisions
diagramStepNotes: In the first week, several verbs repeatedly remain in the bare form even with clear past-time expressions such as last night and yesterday, creating a pattern across dates and lexical items.
Regular forms such as called and checked appear alongside goed and buyed: the emerging past-tense rule produces target forms and is also extended to irregular verbs.

After went and bought enter more prepared writing, new events also bring opened and called. Supervisor feedback is part of the learning process, while the later pattern extends across more lexical items.

The spontaneous phone call differs from the prepared summary in modality, preparation time, attention, and time pressure at once, so he go demonstrates contextual variation but does not prove that pressure alone caused the return.
The manager also checks whether keys, repairs, cash, and ticket numbers were handed over correctly. The language samples and the work results together shape the support plan and independent shifts.
mapping: Early call, give, go, and buy repeatedly describe past events → repetition across verbs weakens the explanation of single-instance carelessness.
called and checked coexist with goed and buyed → as a new rule enters the system, target-like forms and overgeneralizations appear together.
Prepared writing contains went, bought, opened, and called → later output is not merely reproducing the two corrected irregular answers.
The phone call contains he go while written past forms appear during the same period → output from the same learner varies with task and modality conditions.

Formal handovers, original pages, the phone sticky note, and actual handover results are all retained → developmental judgment rests on longitudinal, multi-condition evidence rather than one correct sentence or one return to an earlier form.
module.boundary: Interlanguage is not a random mixture of two languages, and every fluctuation does not represent progress. Task, preparation, attention, pressure, and spoken versus written conditions often change together, so a single story cannot isolate the causal effect of each one. Feedback can also participate in learning. Multiple samples can support a cautious judgment about systematic patterns and variation at that time, but they cannot diagnose the learner’s entire language ability from one performance. The hostel, characters, and language samples are fictional.
module.reflection: Why do the written went and bought and the spoken he go from the same period need to be kept together, rather than using only one kind of performance to conclude that Zhou Ran either “has learned it” or “has gone backward”?

referencesZh.citation: Selinker, L. (1972). Interlanguage. International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching, 10(1–4), 209–232. https://doi.org/10.1515/iral.1972.10.1-4.209
referencesZh.use: 用于支持中介语作为学习者动态而具有系统性的语言系统，以及学习者规则、迁移和可能稳定形式等核心讨论；不为虚构学习者样本背书。

referencesZh.citation: Tarone, E. (2002). Frequency Effects, Noticing, and Creativity: Factors in a Variationist Interlanguage Framework. Studies in Second Language Acquisition, 24(2), 287–296. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0272263102002139
referencesZh.use: 用于支持中介语中的变异、注意、频率与创造性等因素，并提醒不同任务与条件下的形式差异不能简单等同于随机错误或线性进步。

references.citation: Selinker, L. (1972). Interlanguage. International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching, 10(1–4), 209–232. https://doi.org/10.1515/iral.1972.10.1-4.209
references.use: Used to support interlanguage as a dynamic but systematic learner language system, including learner-generated rules, transfer, and the possibility of stabilized forms; it does not provide factual support for the fictional learner samples.

references.citation: Tarone, E. (2002). Frequency Effects, Noticing, and Creativity: Factors in a Variationist Interlanguage Framework. Studies in Second Language Acquisition, 24(2), 287–296. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0272263102002139
references.use: Used to support variation, noticing, frequency, and creativity within a variationist interlanguage framework, and to caution against treating differences across tasks and conditions as either random error or simple linear progress.

articles.title: A Small Change in the Saturday List
articles.summary: Chen He is making the Saturday baking checklist. She has the supplies sorted out, but one word in her English draft sends her back to the voice messages.
articles.summaryZh: 陈禾正在整理周六烘焙清单。东西她都安排明白了，英文草稿里却有一个词，让她回头又听了一遍语音。
storyParagraphs: Chen He belongs to a baking exchange that meets somewhere different each week. This month she is organizing the group’s English voice messages. They will meet at a new member’s home on Saturday, so everyone is reviewing what was missing last week and dividing up the replacements. She hears “I didn’t bring the scale” and puts her own name beside the scale. She also understands that someone did not buy butter and someone else could not find a box. She turns the messages into a checklist, leaving spaces beside the remaining items for people to claim.

That evening, while preparing the English version of the list, she transcribes several messages: didn’t bring, didn’t buy, didn’t find. Her own draft, however, says “Mina didn’t bought butter.” Seeing three sentences with different meanings next to one another makes her stop. She underlines bring, buy, and find, then draws a circle around bought in her own sentence.

The next day, a new member she has not yet met sends “I didn’t know the door code.” Chen He sends the entry code. As she scrolls back through the messages, she pauses at know. She copies it into the margin after bring, buy, and find, then rereads her own checklist. Before sending it, she changes “Mina didn’t bought butter” to “Mina didn’t buy butter” and adds the name of the person bringing butter this week.

On Saturday, they talk about the previous week while weighing flour. Explaining why she was late, Chen He still blurts out “I didn’t took the bus.” The person beside her steadies the flour bag and naturally echoes “I didn’t take the bus.” Chen He repeats the corrected form. When it is her turn to describe the journey home, another past-tense form reaches her lips first; she catches it only halfway through speaking.

At the end of the month, while organizing the records again, she encounters a new sentence: “I didn’t leave it outside.” She underlines leave first. In her own notes, she writes “I didn’t see the message” correctly on one line; on another she first writes “didn’t drove,” then rereads it and changes it to “didn’t drive.” Correct and incorrect forms still alternate.

The checklist sent to the group contains only ingredients, tools, and arrival information. Chen He closes her notebook and slips it into the cloth bag carrying the scale. The four verbs remain together in the margin. The new leave from the end of the month sits on the next line, above the crossed-out drove and the drive written in its place.
storyParagraphsZh: 陈禾参加每周换场地的烘焙交换，这个月轮到她整理群里的英语语音。周六要去新成员家，大家正在回顾上周缺了什么，再分头补齐。她听到“I didn’t bring the scale”，马上把秤记到自己名下；又听懂有人没买黄油、没找到盒子。她把语音里的意思一项项抄成清单，物品后面空着名字，等大家认领。
晚上做英文版清单时，她把几条语音转成文字：didn’t bring、didn’t buy、didn’t find。她自己的草稿却写着“Mina didn’t bought butter”。三个内容不同的句子挨在一起后，她停下来，把bring、buy、find分别划线，又在自己的bought外面画了一个圈。
第二天，一位她还没见过的新成员发来“I didn’t know the door code”。陈禾把门禁码发给对方，往上翻消息时，又停在那个know上。她把它抄在页角，接在bring、buy、find后面，再读了一遍自己的清单。待发送的“Mina didn’t bought butter”被她改成“Mina didn’t buy butter”，黄油一栏后面才接上这周要补带的人。
周六见面，大家边称面粉边聊上周。陈禾说起自己那次迟到，还是脱口说了“I didn’t took the bus”。旁边的人一边扶住面粉袋，一边顺势接了一句“I didn’t take the bus”。陈禾跟着改了一次。等轮到她讲回程，又有一个过去式先跑到嘴边，她说到一半才把它收回去。
月底再整理记录时，她遇到没见过的“I didn’t leave it outside”，先在leave下面划线。自己写备注时，“I didn’t see the message”一次写对；另一句先写成“didn’t drove”，她读回去后改成“didn’t drive”。正确和错误仍交替出现。
最后发进群的清单只有食材、工具和到场信息。陈禾合上笔记本，把它塞进装秤的布袋。页角的四个动词还排在一起；月底新添的leave写在下一行，下面是被划掉的drove和后来补上的drive。
articles.overall: The noticing hypothesis concerns conscious awareness of specific forms in second-language input. Understanding the overall meaning, noticing a grammatical feature, and using it fluently are distinct parts of learning.
articles.overallZh: 注意假说关注学习者何时有意识察觉二语输入中的具体形式。听懂整体意思、察觉一个语法特征和熟练使用它，是需要区分的学习环节。
explanationParagraphs: Schmidt’s noticing hypothesis holds that features in input must be consciously noticed to become intake available for learning. This is a theoretical claim about input entering learning processes; the necessity of noticing and the relevant standard of awareness remain debated.

Noticing and fluent production are different stages. In the story, didn’t + base-form verb is correct. Chen He independently notices didn’t know before receiving later feedback on didn’t take; correcting bought, took, and drove also does not make her spoken production immediately automatic.
explanationParagraphsZh: Schmidt的注意假说认为，输入中的语言特征须被有意识察觉，才能成为供学习加工的摄入（intake）。这是关于输入进入学习加工的理论主张，其必要性和意识标准仍有争议。
察觉与熟练产出是不同阶段。故事里didn’t＋动词原形正确，陈禾先自行注意didn’t know，之后才接受didn’t take的反馈；bought、took、drove的改正也没有让口语立即自动化。

module.intro: A learner can understand what input means before separately noticing a particular linguistic form inside it.
module.diagramTitle: From Understanding the Task to Noticing the Verb Form After didn’t
diagramSteps: Use meaning first to complete the practical arrangement
Notice a repeated form across several inputs
Use previously unseen input to confirm the pattern again
Receive feedback and attempt production
Keep testing the form in new input and new expression
diagramStepNotes: She first uses the voice messages to arrange the scale, butter, and box.
bring, buy, and find all appear after didn’t.
didn’t know comes from a new member, and she notices the base form know on her own.
Later, her spoken didn’t took is recast by another participant as didn’t take.
She later writes see correctly but still has to change drove to drive.
mapping: Completing the list from meaning → understanding the overall input.
Underlining the base-form verbs → conscious noticing of a specific form.
didn’t know → independent new input, not dependent on correction.
Feedback on didn’t take → external feedback after noticing.
Correct and incorrect forms coexisting → noticing does not equal automatic mastery.
module.boundary: The noticing hypothesis is a theoretical claim in second-language acquisition, not a uniquely proven mechanism for all language learning. Noticing a form is also not sufficient to guarantee retention, generalization, or automatic production; practice, memory, feedback, frequency, and opportunities to use the form still affect performance.
module.reflection: When a learner can already understand a sentence, what previously unseen input could you use to tell whether the learner is beginning to notice a linguistic form itself rather than merely remembering a translation or a corrected answer?

moduleZh.intro: 学习者可以先理解输入的意思，之后才把其中一个具体语言形式单独察觉出来。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从听懂任务信息到注意didn’t后的动词形式
diagramSteps: 先靠意义完成实际安排
在多个输入中发现重复形式
用未见过的新输入再次确认
接受反馈并尝试产出
在新输入与表达中继续检验
diagramStepNotes: 她先根据语音安排秤、黄油和盒子。
bring、buy、find都出现在didn’t后。
didn’t know来自新成员，她先自行注意到know原形。
之后口语didn’t took被同伴复述为didn’t take。
后来能写对see，也仍会把drove改回drive。
mapping: 按意思补齐清单 → 理解整体输入。
给原形动词划线 → 有意识察觉具体形式。
didn’t know → 独立的新输入，不依赖纠错。
didn’t take反馈 → 察觉后的外部反馈。
正确与错误并存 → noticing不等于自动掌握。
moduleZh.boundary: 注意假说是第二语言习得中的理论主张，不是所有语言学习都已证明的唯一机制。注意到一个形式也不足以保证记住、泛化或自动产出；练习、记忆、反馈、频率和使用机会仍会影响表现。
moduleZh.reflection: 当学习者已经能听懂一句话时，你会用什么未见过的新输入判断他是否开始单独察觉其中的语言形式，而不只是记住某个翻译或改正答案？

references.citation: Schmidt, R. W. (1990). The Role of Consciousness in Second Language Learning. Applied Linguistics, 11(2), 129–158.
references.use: Supports Schmidt’s original discussion of the noticing hypothesis and the distinction between input and intake; it is treated as a theoretical claim rather than an uncontested conclusion.

references.citation: Robinson, P. (1995). Attention, Memory, and the “Noticing” Hypothesis. Language Learning, 45(2), 283–331.
references.use: Supports the research discussion of attention, memory, and the noticing hypothesis while preserving the theoretical debate.

referencesZh.citation: Schmidt, R. W. (1990). The Role of Consciousness in Second Language Learning. Applied Linguistics, 11(2), 129–158.
referencesZh.use: 支持注意假说原始论述以及input与intake的区分；作为论者主张，不写成无争议定论。

referencesZh.citation: Robinson, P. (1995). Attention, Memory, and the “Noticing” Hypothesis. Language Learning, 45(2), 283–331.
referencesZh.use: 支持注意机制与记忆关系的研究讨论，并保留理论争议。

articles.title: The New Label on the Cabinet Door
articles.summary: A community repair workshop merges the parts cabinets used by two worktables. Lin He chooses the supplier's most precise label, but that afternoon an old glass cabinet door leaves three people standing at one drawer with three different names for the same part.
articles.summaryZh: 社区修理工坊把两张工作桌的零件柜合在一起。林禾选了供应商目录里最准确的标签，下午一扇旧玻璃柜门却让三个人站在同一只抽屉前说起三个名字。
storyParagraphs: At 10:00 on Saturday morning, the community repair workshop was merging the parts cabinets used by the woodworking and framing tables, and the first open-repair session would begin at 2:00 that afternoon. Lin He was relabeling the drawers. The most awkward item was a box of gray plastic spacers: the supplier bag called them “3 mm slotted spacers,” the woodworking volunteers had always called them “swifts,” and the framing table listed them as “size sevens.” The pieces in the two old cabinets were identical in shape, dimensions, and package number.

Lin He checked six months of requisition sheets. “Swift” and “size seven” had each taken people straight to the correct drawer within their own work area. She still decided to make the supplier name the main label on the merged cabinet because ordering and stocktaking used that term. When a new volunteer, Xiao Zhou, arrived, Lin He asked him for “two 3 mm slotted spacers.” He followed the label and retrieved the right pieces immediately. The supplier name itself was neither obscure nor inaccurate.

The first repair that afternoon was an old glass cabinet door. The wooden frame and the glazing strip needed work from both teams. A-Lu held the frame and said, “Get two swifts,” while Yu Lan told Xiao Zhou, “They’re in the size-seven drawer.” Xiao Zhou went to the merged cabinet and saw only “3 mm slotted spacers.” He knew that was the term Lin He had just taught him, but he did not know whether either internal name referred to the same item, so he returned empty-handed to check. The frame was still clamped in the vise, and Yu Lan had to keep holding the glass while they waited.

Lin He brought the original supplier bag to the table. A-Lu recognized the notch and thickness as a “swift”; Yu Lan checked the package number and confirmed that it was the “size seven.” Only then could Xiao Zhou connect all three names to the same box. Before the repair continued, Lin He did not ask either team to change its vocabulary immediately. Instead, she added a temporary bridge label to the drawer: “3 mm slotted spacer | swift | size seven,” with the package number at the far right.

Halfway through the cabinet-door repair, Yu Lan needed another spacer. She still said “size seven,” but this time Xiao Zhou went straight to the drawer marked by the bridge label. A little later, Lin He asked him to add a “3 mm slotted spacer” to the parts tray, and he took one from the same box. Later that afternoon, the woodworking whiteboard still read “swift: 2 short,” while the framing requisition sheet still said “add 1 size seven.” All three names continued to work in the settings where they were shared.

Before closing, Lin He printed the permanent label again. The supplier name and package number were on the first line, with “swift / size seven” in smaller type below. The two old paper labels she had removed that morning were clipped into the label box. Three spacers were missing from the stack in the drawer.
storyParagraphsZh: 星期六上午十点，社区修理工坊要把木工桌和装框桌的零件柜合并，下午两点第一场开放维修就会进人。林禾负责重贴抽屉标签，最麻烦的是一盒灰色塑料垫片：供应商袋上写着“3毫米开槽垫片”，木工桌一直叫它“雨燕”，装框桌的领料单则写“七码”。两边旧柜里的实物、尺寸和包装号完全一样。
林禾查了半年领料单，“雨燕”和“七码”各自在自己的桌边都能直接把人带到正确抽屉。她仍决定先用供应商名称做合柜后的主标签，因为订货、盘点都用这个名称。新志愿者小周刚到时，林禾让他拿“两片3毫米开槽垫片”，他照着标签立刻取对；这个名称本身并不难懂，也没有指错东西。
下午第一件维修是一扇旧玻璃柜门，木框和压条要两组人一起处理。阿鲁扶着木框说“拿两片雨燕”，余岚同时提醒小周“七码那格”。小周走到新柜前，只看见“3毫米开槽垫片”；他知道林禾刚才这样叫过，却不知道两个内部称呼是不是同一件东西，便空手回来确认。台钳还夹着木框，玻璃只能先由余岚扶着等。
林禾把原包装袋放到桌边。阿鲁看缺口和厚度认出“雨燕”，余岚按包装号确认“七码”，小周这才把三个叫法对到同一盒。维修继续前，林禾没有要求两组立刻改口，而是在抽屉上加了一张临时桥接条：“3毫米开槽垫片｜雨燕｜七码”，包装号写在最右边。
柜门装到一半，余岚又要一片。她仍说“七码”，小周这次直接从桥接标签对应的抽屉取出；随后林禾叫他补“3毫米开槽垫片”到托盘，他也取的是同一盒。木工桌晚些时候的白板仍写“雨燕缺2”，装框组领料单仍写“七码补1”，三种名称在各自共享的场合都继续工作。
闭馆前，林禾重新打印正式标签：供应商名称和包装号放在第一行，下面并排保留“雨燕 / 七码”。上午撕下来的两张旧纸条被夹进标签盒，抽屉里那叠灰色垫片少了三片。
explanationParagraphs: The arbitrariness of the sign means that linguistic form and concept are usually not bound by one natural or inevitable connection: the same object can be stably referred to by different forms, and those forms work mainly because a community shares and maintains the association.

“Arbitrary” does not mean that individuals can rename things at will. Even a clear and accurate new form must enter shared use; sound symbolism, iconicity, word formation, historical habit, and the language system also constrain forms.
explanationParagraphsZh: 符号任意性指语言形式与概念之间通常没有天然唯一绑定：同一对象可以由不同形式稳定指称，形式之所以能组织沟通，主要因为共同体共享并延续这种关联。
“任意”不等于个人可随意改名。新形式即使准确清楚，也需要进入共享使用；同时拟声、象似、构词、历史习惯和语言系统都会限制形式。
articles.overall: “3 mm slotted spacer” is accurate and works immediately among people who share it, while “swift” and “size seven” remain effective within their original groups. The cabinet merger does involve change management, but what determines whether a term can organize action immediately is whether speaker and listener share the form–concept relation. The bridge label makes the three conventions explicitly compatible.
articles.overallZh: “3毫米开槽垫片”准确且能在共享它的人之间立即工作，“雨燕”和“七码”也各自在原群体中稳定有效。合柜造成的困难确有变更管理成分，但真正决定一个称呼能否立刻组织协作的，是说者和听者是否共享形式与概念的对应；桥接标签把三套约定显式对齐。

module.intro: The same spacer is called a “swift” at the woodworking table, a “size seven” at the framing table, and something else in the supplier catalog. All three terms can accurately identify the part, but a term coordinates people immediately only after it is shared or explicitly connected to the others.
module.diagramTitle: How a sign form gains stable function through shared convention
diagramSteps: The same object acquires different stable names in different user groups
Each name directly organizes action among people who share it
A new name enters the merged space before its shared range has caught up
A cross-group task exposes the coordination cost of unaligned conventions
Explicit bridging allows several forms to become mutually recognizable in the new shared setting
diagramStepNotes: “Swift,” “size seven,” and the supplier term all refer to the same specification of spacer, so the problem does not come from one word being inaccurate.
Xiao Zhou retrieves the right item immediately when Lin He says “3 mm slotted spacer,” showing that a descriptive term works perfectly once it is shared.
He pauses at “swift / size seven” because he does not yet know how those forms map onto the standard label, not because the object has changed.
Training after a cabinet merger can certainly reduce the cost, but what training does is establish and transmit shared sign-to-concept mappings.
The bridge label makes all three established forms mutually recognizable without declaring any one of them naturally bound to the object.
mapping: The same box of gray spacers → the conceptual object remains unchanged.
“Swift,” “size seven,” and “3 mm slotted spacer” → several forms can all stably and accurately refer to the same object.
Xiao Zhou can act on the supplier term but cannot immediately equate the two older terms → usable meaning depends on shared mapping, not on which name seems more natural.
The delay during the glass-cabinet repair → unaligned conventions create a visible coordination cost.
The permanent bridge label → the merged community restores coordination by explicitly aligning existing terms with the standard name.
module.boundary: The arbitrariness of the sign does not mean that all names are equally good or that individuals can assign meanings however they like. Sound symbolism, iconicity, word formation, historical convention, and internal system relations can all constrain forms; organizational training and labeling also affect how quickly a convention becomes shared. This fictional workshop is only a concrete model and does not empirically establish that all linguistic signs are arbitrary to the same degree.
module.reflection: Why could Xiao Zhou immediately retrieve the correct item when he heard “3 mm slotted spacer,” while “swift” and “size seven,” which referred just as accurately to the same item, first had to be linked to it for him?

moduleZh.intro: 同一种垫片在木工桌叫“雨燕”，在装框桌叫“七码”，供应商又给了它一个技术名称。三个称呼都能准确指向实物，但只有进入共同使用或被明确对齐后，才会让不同的人立即采取同一个行动。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 符号形式怎样靠共享约定获得稳定功能
diagramSteps: 同一对象在不同使用群体中形成不同稳定称呼
每种称呼在共享它的成员之间都能直接组织行动
新名称进入合并后的共同空间，但共享范围尚未同步
跨群体任务使未对齐的形式关系产生协调成本
显式桥接后，多套称呼可在新的共同体中被共同识别
diagramStepNotes: “雨燕”“七码”和供应商名称都指向同一规格垫片，问题不来自某个词本身不准确。
小周按“3毫米开槽垫片”立即取对，说明描述性名称一旦共享同样能稳定发挥作用。
他听到“雨燕／七码”时停下来，是因为尚不知道这些形式与柜上标准名的对应，而不是物件变了。
合柜培训当然能减少成本，但培训之所以有用，正是因为它建立和传播共同的符号对应关系。
桥接标签让三种既有形式共同可识别，并不宣告其中某一个与物件天然绑定。
mapping: 同一盒灰色垫片 → 概念对象保持不变。
“雨燕”“七码”“3毫米开槽垫片” → 多个形式都可以准确稳定地指向同一对象。
小周能按供应商名取对、却不能立即把两个旧称等同 → 可用意义取决于共享对应，而非名称是否更自然。
玻璃柜门维修中的等待 → 未对齐的约定产生真实协调成本。
正式桥接标签 → 新共同体通过共享规则把原有称呼与标准名对齐。
moduleZh.boundary: 符号任意性不等于所有名称质量相同，也不等于个人能随意规定词义。拟声、象似、构词、历史习惯和系统内部关系会限制形式；组织培训和标签管理也会影响共享速度。本故事是虚构工坊，只提供一个可感模型，不能据此实证所有语言符号都同样任意。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么小周听到“3毫米开槽垫片”时能立刻取对，而同样准确指向这件物品的“雨燕”和“七码”却必须先建立对应关系？

references.citation: Saussure, F. de. (2011). Course in General Linguistics. Translated by Wade Baskin; edited by Perry Meisel and Haun Saussy. Columbia University Press.
references.use: Used to support the idea that linguistic form and concept are generally not linked by one natural or necessary bond, and that linguistic meaning depends on a socially shared sign system; “arbitrary” is not treated as meaning that individuals may name things however they wish.

references.citation: Joseph, J. E. (2004). The Linguistic Sign. In The Cambridge Companion to Saussure, pp. 59–75. Cambridge University Press.
references.use: Used to support the understanding of linguistic signs as part of a socially shared system and the idea that arbitrary form–concept associations are still constrained by community use and systemic relations; it does not provide evidence for the fictional workshop.

articles.title: The Sentence She Could Not Hear
articles.summary: Before five, Jo Ann must recut an audio story about a student searching for her bow just before a performance. The first version tells the listener everything the backstage team knows, making the person who is still searching sound unreasonable.
articles.summaryZh: 五点前，乔安必须重剪一段学生上台前找不到琴弓的录音。第一版把后台知道的事全说了出来，于是听众反倒觉得那个正在寻找的人毫无道理。
storyParagraphs: On Wednesday afternoon, the community theater had to deliver a four-minute anniversary audio piece before 5:00. Jo Ann chose the few minutes before a performance when student cellist Xiao Lan could not find her bow. But during a test listen to the first version, a colleague asked, “If everyone already knew the bow was in the costume room, why did she keep looking?” Jo Ann reopened the project and saw that she had given the listener information from several backstage channels all at once, making Xiao Lan’s urgency sound unreasonable.

She laid the material out again in order: 18:39, 18:40, 18:41, and onward. At 18:40, what Xiao Lan actually heard was the zipper of the empty bow case, a stage-call reminder, and a classmate saying, “You still had it in your hand just now.” On another headset channel at the same time, someone reported that a bow had been found in the costume room, but Xiao Lan was not wearing that channel. Jo Ann kept 18:40 in its original time position and simply left the backstage channel that Xiao Lan could not hear out of the finished audio at that point.

From 18:41 to 18:42, Xiao Lan first went back to the practice room, then asked around at stage left, and in a voice message guessed that she might have left the bow in the auditorium. The backstage log already said that “a lost item was received in the costume room.” In the narration, Jo Ann gave only the time and the phrase “backstage logged a lost item,” without telling listeners that it was the bow. The narrator’s voice did not change, but the judgments available through that narration stayed close to the information Xiao Lan herself could access.

At 18:43, a stage-left assistant told Xiao Lan directly, “Your bow has been found. It’s on its way over.” This was the first time she actually received the answer. Only from that moment did Jo Ann widen the information field: the next line of narration explained that the stage manager had learned earlier, on another channel, that the costume room had found the bow. The original 18:40 backstage radio clip remained in the project library and was not moved to 18:43 and presented as if it had happened then.

After 18:44, Xiao Lan had the bow back and was preparing to go onstage. Jo Ann then shifted the focalization explicitly to the stage manager. On the work channel, the team was checking the movement of costume-change bags: the bow had been leaning beside one of them and had been carried into the costume room with it. The shift did not tell listeners that Xiao Lan should have known earlier. Instead, it opened another worker’s field of perception and turned the same few minutes from a personal search into a backstage object-flow problem.

At 4:52, Jo Ann exported the third version. On the timeline, 18:39, 18:40, 18:41, 18:43, and 18:44 remained in order, and the same third-person narrator ran through the entire piece. The 18:40 backstage radio clip that Xiao Lan could not hear was still sitting unused in the project track library. Jo Ann renamed the file “Anniversary_audio_v3,” and the progress bar reached 100%.
storyParagraphsZh: 星期三下午，社区剧场五点前必须交出一段四分钟周年音频。乔安选了学生大提琴手小岚演出前找不到琴弓的几分钟，可第一版试听时，同事问：“既然大家早知道琴弓在服装间，她为什么还一直找？”乔安回到工程文件，发现自己把后台不同频道掌握的信息全铺给了听众，小岚的着急因此像没来由。
她把素材按18:39、18:40、18:41往后重新排。18:40这一格里，小岚实际听到的是琴盒拉链、走台催促和同伴一句“刚才还在你手上”；另一条耳机频道同时有人报告服装间发现一把琴弓，但小岚没戴那一路耳机。乔安让18:40继续保留在原时间位置，只从最终音频里拿掉她当时无法听见的后台频道。
18:41到18:42，小岚先回练习室，又在侧台问人，语音里还猜“是不是落在观众席”。后台记录此时已经写下“服装间收到遗落物”，乔安在旁白里只报时间和“后台登记了一件遗落物”，不替听众点明是琴弓。旁白声音没变，但描述能给出的判断仍被限制在小岚当时可获得的范围附近。
18:43，侧台助理当面对小岚说：“你的弓找到了，正在送过来。”这是她第一次真正得到答案。乔安从这一刻才扩大音频的信息范围：下一句旁白说明，舞台经理比她更早从另一频道知道服装间发现了琴弓。那段18:40的后台原始对讲仍留在工程素材库里，没有被挪到18:43伪装成现在发生的声音。
18:44以后，小岚拿回琴弓，准备上台。乔安随后明确把焦点转到舞台经理：工作频道里正在核对服装袋流转，原来琴弓曾靠在换场袋边，被一起带进服装间。这个转换给出的不是“小岚早该知道”的答案，而是另一名工作人员当时能看见的物件路径，让同一事件从个人寻找变成后台流转问题。
四点五十二，乔安导出第三版。时间线上18:39、18:40、18:41、18:43、18:44依次排开，同一个第三人称旁白贯穿全段；18:40那条小岚听不到的后台对讲仍停在素材库未启用轨。文件名改成“Anniversary_audio_v3”，进度条走到100%。
explanationParagraphs: Focalization concerns whose range of information, perception, and judgment enters a narrative; it is different from the question of who narrates. The same narrative voice can be limited to what one character sees, knows, or misunderstands, and can later move to another range.

Focalization changes what readers or listeners can use to make judgments. Information from several people can all be true without any one character possessing the whole picture at the time; chronological order, narrative voice, and field of knowledge are separate dimensions.
explanationParagraphsZh: 叙事聚焦关注信息、感知和判断经由谁的范围进入故事，与“谁在讲述”不同。同一个叙述声音可以受限于某个角色所见、所知和所误解，也可在之后移动到另一范围。
聚焦改变读者依据什么作判断。多方信息可以都真实，但不等于任何角色当时拥有完整图景；时间顺序、叙述声音与可知范围是不同维度。
articles.overall: The third version does not move the 18:40 backstage message to 18:43. At 18:40, the finished piece contains only information Xiao Lan could actually access. Once she learns at 18:43 that the bow has been found, the narrative field widens; at 18:44 it explicitly shifts to the stage manager, and a new understanding comes from another person’s visible path of the object. Timeline, narrator, and focal field are therefore handled separately.
articles.overallZh: 第三版没有把18:40的后台消息挪到18:43，而是让18:40仍只出现小岚实际可得的信息；她18:43获知琴弓找到后，叙述范围才扩大。18:44再明确转向舞台经理，新的理解来自另一人的可见物件路径。时间线、叙述声音和聚焦范围因此被分别处理。

module.intro: The same narrator can follow one chronological timeline while admitting only what a particular character could perceive, know, and use to judge at that moment. The field can widen when the character receives new information, and a shift to another focalizer can change how the same event is understood.
module.diagramTitle: How narrative voice, chronological order, and focal field organize information separately
diagramSteps: Keep events in their actual time positions and first ask who can perceive what at each moment
Make sounds, wording, and judgments stay within the current focalizer’s field of knowledge
Information held by other characters at the same moment may be true but remain outside the narration for now
When the current character gains new information, widen what may enter the narrative
Shift focalization explicitly so another field of knowledge can produce a new relational understanding
diagramStepNotes: 18:40 remains at 18:40; the earlier radio clip is not moved later to create a false chronology. What changes is whether that channel belongs to Xiao Lan’s perceptual field.
The same third-person narrator remains throughout, showing that narrator and focalizer are separate dimensions.
The narration says only “backstage logged a lost item” rather than naming the bow, so the narrator’s wording also respects the current information boundary.
After Xiao Lan hears the news herself at 18:43, the narration can state that the stage manager knew earlier; the field widens only after her knowledge changes.
At 18:44, the focus explicitly moves to the stage manager’s view of object movement, adding a new interpretation rather than merely revealing an answer that had been withheld.
mapping: At 18:40, only the zipper, stage call, and classmate’s words that Xiao Lan can hear are used → chronology remains intact while the information entrance is focalized.
The unused backstage radio track → information can be true and available to the editor without having to enter the narrative immediately.
The same third-person narrator → “who speaks” does not change simply because the focal field changes.
The narrative widens after Xiao Lan learns the news at 18:43 → a change in character knowledge changes what information may enter.
The shift to the stage manager at 18:44 → moving focalization reveals an object-flow relation that Xiao Lan could not previously perceive.
module.boundary: Focalization is not merely delaying an answer, and it does not require chronology to be disrupted. It describes whose field of information, perception, and judgment enters a narrative. Focalization may remain fixed, move, or combine perspectives, and a character’s perspective may itself be limited or mistaken. The theater and audio materials in this story are fictional and serve only as a conceptual entry point, not as a narratology experiment or universal template.
module.reflection: Why can the 18:40 backstage radio message be completely true without needing to be heard in the 18:40 finished audio, while the narrative can reasonably widen after 18:43?

moduleZh.intro: 同一个旁白可以沿着同一条时间线讲述，却只让某个角色当时能感知、知道和据以判断的信息进入。角色真正获得新消息后，信息范围才能扩大；转向另一名角色时，故事对同一事件的理解也随之改变。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 叙述声音、时间顺序与聚焦范围如何分别组织信息
diagramSteps: 保持事件的时间位置，先确定谁在该时刻能感知什么
让声音、措辞和判断不越过当前聚焦者的可知范围
同一时刻其他角色拥有的信息可以真实存在但暂不进入叙述
当前角色获得新信息后，再扩大可进入的内容
明确转换聚焦者，让另一范围带来新的关系理解
diagramStepNotes: 18:40仍位于18:40，没有把早先录音后移来制造时间假象；变化是那条频道是否属于小岚的感知范围。
同一第三人称旁白始终存在，说明叙述者和聚焦者可以分离。
“后台登记了一件遗落物”不点明琴弓，使旁白的知识呈现也服从当前信息边界。
18:43小岚亲自获知后，叙述才说明舞台经理更早知道；范围扩大建立在角色知识变化之后。
18:44明确转向舞台经理的物件流转视野，带来新的理解，而不是仅补一个此前藏起来的答案。
mapping: 18:40只播小岚能听见的拉链、催场和同伴话语 → 时间顺序保持，信息入口受聚焦限制。
未启用的后台对讲轨 → 真实存在的信息不等于必须立刻进入叙述。
同一第三人称旁白 → “谁讲述”没有随着聚焦范围一起变化。
18:43小岚获得消息后叙述扩大 → 角色知识变化改变可进入信息。
18:44转向舞台经理 → 聚焦移动使听众看到此前不可见的物件流转关系。
moduleZh.boundary: 叙事聚焦不等于把答案故意拖后，也不要求时间顺序被打乱。它描述信息、感知和判断经由谁的范围进入叙述；聚焦可固定、移动或组合，角色视角也可能有限或错误。本故事中的剧场与音频均为虚构，只提供概念入口，不是叙事学实验或普遍模板。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么18:40的后台对讲即使真实存在，也不必在18:40的成片里让听众听见，而18:43以后叙述又可以合理扩大？

references.citation: Bal, M. (1985). Focalization. In Narratology: Introduction to the Theory of Narrative, pp. 100–114. University of Toronto Press.
references.use: Used to support focalization as a question of how narrative information, perception, and judgment are organized, including the distinction between the focalizing agent and what is perceived; it does not provide evidence for the fictional audio material.

references.citation: University of Tübingen. Focalisation.
references.use: Used to support the distinction between “who sees/perceives” and “who speaks,” and the idea that focalization can be limited, shifted, or combined; chronological order and focal field are not treated as the same dimension.

referencesZh.citation: Bal, M. (1985). Focalization. In Narratology: Introduction to the Theory of Narrative, pp. 100–114. University of Toronto Press.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持聚焦作为叙事信息、感知与判断的组织问题，并区分聚焦主体与被感知对象；不为虚构音频材料背书。

referencesZh.citation: University of Tübingen. Focalisation.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持“谁看见／感知”与“谁说话”的区分，以及聚焦可限制、移动或组合；不把时间顺序与聚焦范围视为同一维度。

articles.title: There’s Another Group at Ten
articles.summary: The choir must clear the hall by 9:45, and a dance class enters at ten. Su Ning gives the conductor a brief reminder about the time; a volunteer coiling cables at the back hears it too. Minutes later, the main speaker needed by the next group is dark.
articles.summaryZh: 合唱团必须在九点四十五前撤场，舞蹈班十点进门。苏宁对指挥说了一句时间提醒，后排收线的人也听见了；几分钟后，下一组要用的主音箱已经断电。
storyParagraphs: On Thursday night, the choir had to finish clearing the community hall by 9:45, and the dance class would enter at 10:00 sharp. Facilities coordinator Su Ning needed to leave the main speaker booked by the dance class and an open floor, while removing the choir’s own music stands, microphones, cups, and coats. At 9:25, the conductor asked whether they could sing the final piece once more from the beginning. Su Ning looked at the clock and said only to him, “There’s another group at ten.” The conductor changed the plan from a full run to the last eight bars.

A sound volunteer working at the back also heard the sentence, although it had not been addressed to him. He had come in temporarily to help with teardown, and the choir checklist in his hand followed the usual practice: after a performance, the group cleared its microphones, cables, and sound area. On most Thursdays, no later group continued using the equipment. Tonight’s exception—the dance class had rented the main speaker—was written on a separate venue equipment sheet posted on the side wall, while he was facing away from it and coiling cables.

Seeing the conductor shorten rehearsal and everyone speed up, he interpreted the overheard reference to “the next group” as meaning “clear the space for them as quickly as possible.” At 9:38, he unplugged the main speaker and had already coiled half of the first shared audio cable. Su Ning came back from the equipment room and found the speaker dark. Reconnecting it, powering it up, and running a test would take at least four minutes, and the dance class needed that speaker immediately for warm-up music.

Su Ning walked over, flipped the side-wall equipment sheet to the line reading “Dance class: main speaker ×1,” and put one hand on the second cable he was about to unplug. This time she looked directly at him and said, “There’s another group at ten.” Following her hand, the volunteer looked at the equipment sheet and asked, “So the main speaker stays?” Su Ning said, “Yes.” He put the half-coiled shared cable back down and continued removing only the choir’s two microphones and extension lead.

Four minutes were already gone. At 9:43, several folding chairs were still blocking the side entrance, and members of the dance class had begun waiting outside. Su Ning did not use another indirect reminder. She told the parents moving the chairs, “They come in through the side door. Clear this first.” The chairs were moved to the equipment-room entrance. At 9:47, the sound volunteer finished a ten-second test; the dance teacher heard the speaker working normally and kept the students outside to change shoes rather than asking to enter early.

At 9:58, the last choir music stand went into the equipment room. The side-door passage was clear, the main speaker was still powered on, and the choir’s two microphones were packed away. At exactly 10:00, the dance teacher pressed play, and the first warm-up track came through the speaker that had just been reconnected.
storyParagraphsZh: 周四晚上，社区礼堂九点四十五必须完成合唱团撤场，十点舞蹈班准时进来。场务苏宁要留下舞蹈班预订的主音箱和整块空地，同时收走合唱团自己的谱架、话筒、杯子和外套。九点二十五，指挥问能不能把最后一首从头再唱一遍。苏宁看了钟，只对他说：“十点还有下一组。”指挥把整首改成只排最后八小节。
后排的音响志愿者也听见了，但这句话并不是对他说的。他临时来帮撤场，手里的合唱团清单沿用平常做法：演出结束后把本组话筒、线材和音响区域清空；多数周四，后面没有另一组继续使用设备。今晚舞蹈班租用主音箱的例外写在场地方另一张设备单上，贴在侧墙，他当时正背对那边收线。
看见指挥缩短排练、大家开始加快动作，他便把旁听到的“下一组”理解成“给后面的人尽快腾空”。九点三十八，他拔掉主音箱电源，把第一根公共音频线卷到一半。苏宁从器材间回来才发现音箱灭了；重新接线、开机和测试至少要四分钟，而舞蹈班一进来就要用它放热身音乐。
苏宁走到他身边，把侧墙设备单翻到“舞蹈班：主音箱×1”，一只手按住他正要拔的第二根线。这次她直接对着他说：“十点还有下一组。”志愿者顺着她的手看到设备单，问：“所以主音箱留？”苏宁答“对”。他把卷到一半的公共线放回，只收合唱团自己的两支话筒和延长线。
四分钟已经花掉。九点四十三，几把折叠椅还堵着侧门，舞蹈班有人提前到门外等。苏宁没有继续用含蓄提醒，而是对搬椅子的家长说：“他们从侧门进，先把这里清出来。”家长把椅子推到器材间门口；九点四十七，音响志愿者重新跑完十秒测试，舞蹈老师听见声音正常，带学生先在门外换鞋。
九点五十八，最后一只谱架进入器材间。侧门走道空了，主音箱仍通着电，两支合唱团话筒已经装箱。十点整，舞蹈老师按下播放键，第一段热身音乐从刚才重新接好的音箱里响起来。
explanationParagraphs: Pragmatics studies how listeners combine literal meaning, addressee, shared knowledge, relationships, timing, and the immediate task to infer what an utterance is doing in that situation. The same literal content can carry different implied actions in different contexts.

Pragmatic inference is not arbitrary guessing and does not always succeed. When shared background is incomplete, a reasonable listener can still misunderstand; in high-stakes or time-pressured situations, saying things directly is often better.
explanationParagraphsZh: 语用学研究听者怎样结合字面意义、说话对象、共同知识、关系、时机和现场任务，推断一句话在这里要完成什么行动。同一句字面内容可在不同情境中承担不同言外作用。
语用推断不是任意猜测，也不保证成功。共享背景不足时，合理听者也可能误解；高风险或赶时间时，直接说明往往更好。
articles.overall: The first “There’s another group at ten” is a reply to the conductor, while the sound volunteer only overhears it and reasonably interprets it through the hall’s usual teardown practice. The second time, the utterance is addressed directly to him, and the equipment sheet, Su Ning’s hand on the cable, and their shared object of attention complete the context. Only then does the same literal sentence narrow to “the next group needs the main speaker.” The misunderstanding costs about four minutes.
articles.overallZh: 第一次“十点还有下一组”是对指挥的回应，音响志愿者只是旁听，并依据礼堂惯常撤场方式作出合理却错误的推断。第二次话语直接面向他，设备单、苏宁按住线缆和共同注意对象补齐语境，才把相同字面内容收窄为“下一组要用主音箱”。误解真实消耗了四分钟。

module.intro: “There's another group at ten” supplies stable literal information, but it does not by itself say what should be removed or left in place. The conductor and the overhearing volunteer infer different actions from different task backgrounds. Their understanding aligns only when the equipment sheet, cable, and intended addressee become jointly clear.
module.diagramTitle: How pragmatic inference is constrained jointly by literal meaning and shared context
diagramSteps: An utterance first provides stable literal content within a specific speaking situation
Different listeners combine it with the shared background actually available to them
When background information is incomplete, a reasonable inference can still be wrong
A new shared object of attention and new evidence can revise the earlier inference
After a costly misunderstanding, the speaker can switch to more direct language
diagramStepNotes: The first “There’s another group at ten” clearly answers the conductor’s request to extend rehearsal, so interpreting it as a refusal is natural for the conductor.

The sound volunteer only overhears it and relies on the usual Thursday practice of clearing the whole sound area; the rental exception is neither on his checklist nor in his line of sight at that moment.
He unplugs the main speaker not because he ignores shared information, but because the relevant exception has not yet become part of the background he shares.
The second time, Su Ning addresses him directly, holds the cable, and turns the equipment sheet to the relevant line; the literal sentence and shared focus together support “leave the main speaker.”

The four-minute recovery reduces the time available for the rest of the changeover, and Su Ning then states the side-door requirement directly, showing that pragmatic competence does not mean preferring indirectness.
mapping: The conductor asks to sing the full piece again → the scheduling statement functions as an indirect refusal in that exchange.
The overhearing volunteer begins unplugging the main speaker based on normal teardown practice → pragmatic inference depends on the shared knowledge actually available to the listener.
Tonight’s rental exception is not salient at first → a reasonable inference can still fail when shared background is incomplete.
The equipment sheet, Su Ning’s hand on the cable, and direct address → new shared evidence constrains and revises the implied action.
Su Ning later says directly, “They come in through the side door” → clear explicit language and pragmatic inference are not opposites, and directness can be better when time is costly.
module.boundary: Pragmatics is not simply “reading the room,” and it does not imply that indirect wording is more sophisticated. Inference is constrained by literal content, addressee, shared knowledge, relationships, timing, and situational evidence, and it can fail, be manipulated, or require clarification. The hall and characters are fictional; the four-minute rework is a concrete cost of pragmatic misunderstanding, and direct explanation is often preferable in critical tasks.
module.reflection: Why was the sound volunteer’s first interpretation reasonable at the time, while seeing the equipment sheet and jointly attending to the same cable made the very same sentence support the opposite action?

moduleZh.intro: “十点还有下一组”提供了稳定的字面信息，却没有单独说出此刻该收什么、该留下什么。指挥和旁听的志愿者依据不同的任务背景作出不同推断；直到设备单、线缆和说话对象同时明确，行动含义才重新对齐。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 语用推断如何由字面内容与共享情境共同约束
diagramSteps: 一句话先提供稳定的字面内容和明确说话场合
不同听者结合自己可得的共同背景推断言外行动
背景信息不足时，合理推断也可能产生误解
新的共同注意对象与证据可以修正先前推断
高时间成本出现后，说话者可改用更直接表达
diagramStepNotes: 第一次“十点还有下一组”明确回应指挥的延长请求，因此对指挥而言形成拒绝很自然。
志愿者只是旁听，并依据多数周四整套撤场的经验理解“赶紧腾空”；租赁例外不在他手中的清单上，也不在当时视线内。
主音箱被拔并非因为他无视已共享信息，而是因为相关例外尚未进入他的共同背景。
第二次苏宁直接面向他、按住线缆并翻到设备单，字面句与共同注意对象一起使推断转向“主音箱留下”。
四分钟返工压缩后续换场，苏宁随后对侧门问题直接说清，表明语用能力不等于追求含蓄。
mapping: 指挥提出再唱整首 → 同一句排程事实在当前对话中承担拒绝延长的作用。
旁听者依据平常整套撤场开始拔音箱 → 语用推断依赖听者实际拥有的共同知识。
今晚租赁信息当时不显眼可得 → 合理推断仍可能因共享背景不完整而失败。
设备单、按住线缆和直接面向志愿者 → 新的共享线索约束并修正言外理解。
后续改用“他们从侧门进”直接说明 → 清楚表达与语用推断并不对立，时间代价高时直说更有效。
moduleZh.boundary: 语用学不等于“会察言观色”，也不意味着含糊表达更高级。推断受字面内容、说话对象、共同知识、关系、时机和现场证据约束，也可能失败、被操纵或需要澄清。本故事中的礼堂与人物均为虚构；四分钟返工正是语用误解的现实代价，关键任务中直接说明常常更合适。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么音响志愿者第一次的理解在当时是合理的，而第二次看到设备单并和苏宁共同看着同一根线后，同一句话却支持了相反的现场动作？

references.citation: Grice, H. P. (1975). Logic and Conversation. In Peter Cole and Jerry L. Morgan (eds.), Syntax and Semantics, Vol. 3: Speech Acts, pp. 41–58.
references.use: Used to support the distinction between what is said and what is implicated, the cooperative principle, and the derivation of conversational implicature; the maxims are not treated as mechanical rules that real conversations must always obey, nor is inference assumed to succeed automatically.

references.citation: Korta, K., & Perry, J. (2023). Pragmatics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
references.use: Used to support the role of literal content, speaker intention, shared knowledge, addressee, and context in pragmatic interpretation, while preserving room for misunderstanding, clarification, and theoretical disagreement.

referencesZh.citation: Grice, H. P. (1975). Logic and Conversation. In Peter Cole and Jerry L. Morgan (eds.), Syntax and Semantics, Vol. 3: Speech Acts, pp. 41–58.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持“所说”与“所暗含”的区分、合作原则及会话含义的推导；不把准则写成现实交流必须机械服从的命令，也不假定推断必然成功。

referencesZh.citation: Korta, K., & Perry, J. (2023). Pragmatics. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持字面内容、说话者意图、共同知识、说话对象和语境在语用理解中的作用，并保留误解、澄清及理论争议。

articles.title: The Laser Cutter’s Last Ninety Minutes
articles.titleZh: 最后九十分钟的切割机
articles.summary: On Friday afternoon, Chen Wei leans two acrylic sheets beside the makerspace laser cutter. Only ninety minutes remain: the left sheet is for twenty-four tactile signs needed on Saturday, and the right for six connectors a client expects to test on Monday.
articles.summaryZh: 周五下午，陈未把两块透明板靠在创客室的切割机旁。机器只剩九十分钟：左边是周六要装的二十四块触觉标牌，右边是周一客户要试的六个连接件。
storyParagraphs: At 3:00 on Friday afternoon, Chen Wei leaned two acrylic sheets beside the laser cutter at the community makerspace. The machine would shut down for maintenance at 4:30 and stay closed over the weekend. The sheet on the left was to become twenty-four tactile room signs for installation in the community reading corner on Saturday morning; the one on the right was to become six folding display-frame connectors that the client had originally planned to handle and test during Monday’s presentation. Both design files were finished, and all the materials were ready.

She ran both layouts through the time-estimation software. The connectors would take sixty-five minutes and the signs seventy-two, so either job could be completed before 4:30, but there was no way to finish both. The reading-corner team had already prepared temporary printed labels, so it could still open on Saturday without the acrylic signs. The client had also confirmed that Monday’s meeting could proceed with the cardboard model, but without the connectors they could not test on the spot whether the joints would wobble. Both paths remained workable; they simply postponed different things.

Chen Wei left the connector file on the screen, her finger already touching “Start.” Then the reading-corner coordinator called: the handrail installer and several volunteers were already booked for 9:00 on Saturday, and missing that window would mean rescheduling everyone. She ended the call, looked once more at the client’s email, moved the acrylic sheet for the connectors over to the wall, and loaded the sheet for the signs instead. At 4:22, the last sign dropped into the collection tray.

On Saturday morning, all twenty-four signs were mounted on doorframes and the ends of bookcases, and the prepared paper labels stayed unopened. After the last sign was fixed in place, a regular visitor traced the raised dots and found the direction to the restroom. As Chen Wei packed away the empty wrapping, her phone showed a reminder for Monday’s meeting; back at the makerspace, the acrylic sheet that could have been cut into connectors in sixty-five minutes was still standing untouched against the wall.

At Monday’s meeting, the cardboard model could fold and stand, but it could not answer whether the real connectors would wobble under load. The client did not reject the proposal; they simply moved “confirm connection method” from Monday’s agenda to Wednesday, when they could see the physical parts before deciding whether to change the frame width. The rest of the discussion continued as planned, and Chen Wei received the next set of revision notes. By the time she left the meeting room, she had already booked another laser-cutter slot for Wednesday afternoon.

On Tuesday evening, she returned to the makerspace and set the uncut acrylic sheet on the rack beside the machine. She stuck on a label: “Connectors — Wednesday.” Behind it, the empty wrapping from the twenty-four tactile signs was still folded on top of the recycling bin.
storyParagraphsZh: 周五下午三点，陈未把两块透明板靠到社区创客室的激光切割机旁。四点半机器停机维护，周末不开。左边那块要切成二十四块触觉房间标牌，周六上午装进社区阅读角；右边那块要切六个折叠展架连接件，周一客户来时原本要亲手试折。两套文件都已完成，材料也在手边。
她先后把两份排版送进估时软件。连接件六十五分钟，标牌七十二分钟，任何一套都能在四点半前完整切完，但两套放在一起肯定来不及。阅读角负责人已经准备了临时打印纸，若今天不切标牌，周六仍能开门；客户也确认纸板模型足以继续周一会议，但没有连接件就无法现场确认卡合是否会晃。两个方案都能继续，只是会把不同事情推后。
陈未先让连接件文件停在屏幕上，手指已经碰到“开始”。这时阅读角负责人打来电话：周六九点的扶手安装和几名志愿者都已约好，错过这次要重新排人。她挂掉电话，又看了一眼客户邮件，然后把右边那块连接件透明板挪到墙边，换上标牌板。四点二十二分，最后一块标牌落进接料盘。
周六上午，二十四块标牌被装到门框和书架端头，准备好的打印纸没有拆封。最后一块固定好后，一位常客沿着凸点摸到洗手间方向。陈未收起空包装时，手机跳出周一会议提醒；工作室里，那块能在六十五分钟内切完的透明板仍完整靠在墙边。
周一会议上，纸板模型能折、能站，却回答不了真实连接件受力后会不会晃。客户没有否掉方案，只把“连接方式确认”从当天议程挪到周三，等实物出来再决定是否改结构宽度。其余讨论照常结束，陈未也拿到了下一步修改意见。她离开会议室时，周三下午的切割机时段已经重新约好。
周二晚上，她回到创客室，把那块未切的透明板放上机台旁的架子，贴上“连接件—周三”。透明板背后，二十四块标牌留下的空包装纸还折在回收箱最上面。
explanationParagraphs: Opportunity cost is the value of the best feasible alternative forgone when a scarce resource is used one way. It is not the cash price and not the sum of every option that was not chosen.
It arises when the choice is made. Later regret, accidents, or sunk costs are different; later outcomes can only make the value of the forgone alternative easier to see.
explanationParagraphsZh: 机会成本是选择一种稀缺资源用途时，被放弃的最佳可行替代方案的价值。它不等于现金支出，也不等于所有没选方案相加。
它在选择发生时就产生。后来出现的遗憾、意外或沉没成本不是同一概念；后续结果只能让原先放弃的替代价值更容易看见。
articles.overall: The ninety-minute Friday slot was long enough to finish either the signs or the connectors, so the connectors were a real and valuable alternative rather than a task that was never feasible. Choosing the signs was not a mistake, but it also meant giving up the chance to test physical connectors on Monday. Monday merely made visible an opportunity cost that had already arisen with Friday’s choice.
articles.overallZh: 周五九十分钟能完整切标牌，也能完整切连接件，因此连接件是真实而有价值的替代，而不是本来就做不完的次要任务。陈未选择标牌并非错误决定，但这一选择同时放弃了周一可进行的实物卡合确认；周一只是让周五已经产生的机会成本具体显现。

module.intro: Ninety minutes is enough to cut either the signs or the connectors, but not both. Each use is feasible and has near-term value, so committing the same slot to one necessarily postpones the other.
module.diagramTitle: How one choice over a scarce resource creates opportunity cost
diagramSteps: Identify the genuinely scarce resource and how much of it is available
Confirm that several uses are actually feasible at the moment of choice
Commit the resource to one of those uses
Identify the best feasible alternative displaced by that choice
Separate the value of that forgone alternative from later accidental losses
diagramStepNotes: The scarce resource is the final ninety minutes on Friday; the fact that the machine is free does not create more time.
The signs require 72 minutes and the connectors 65 minutes, with both files and materials ready, so the connectors were not a job that was impossible to finish.
When Chen Wei moves the connector sheet to the wall and starts the sign file, the resource allocation has been made.
The connectors have clear value for Monday’s physical fit test, making them the best feasible alternative rather than an unimportant backup task.
The delayed Monday confirmation only makes that value visible; the opportunity cost already arose on Friday when the choice was made.
mapping: The last ninety minutes → scarce machine capacity with no cash price.
Twenty-four tactile room signs → the chosen use of the resource.
Six display-frame connectors → a feasible and genuinely valuable best alternative.
No physical fit test on Monday → a later manifestation of the value of the forgone alternative.
The acrylic sheet labeled “Connectors — Wednesday” → the alternative can still be completed later, but Friday’s opportunity has passed.
module.boundary: Opportunity cost is not simply another name for deadline prioritization, nor is it the sum of every unfinished project. Even a reasonable choice can have an opportunity cost; what matters is whether a genuinely feasible and valuable best alternative existed at the moment of choice. The makerspace, characters, and projects in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why can making the signs first be a reasonable decision while still meaning that Chen Wei gave up the opportunity value of having the physical connectors available on Monday?

moduleZh.intro: 九十分钟足以切完标牌，也足以切完连接件，却不足以完成两者。两项用途都真实可行，也都有近期价值；无论选哪一个，同一时段都会把另一个用途推迟。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 稀缺资源的一次选择怎样形成机会成本
diagramSteps: 确认真正稀缺的资源和可用数量
确认多个用途在选择当下都实际可行
把资源投入其中一个用途
识别因此被放弃的最佳可行替代
把该替代的价值与后来的偶发损失区分开
diagramStepNotes: 周五最后九十分钟是稀缺资源；机器免费并不增加可用时间。
标牌需72分钟、连接件需65分钟，文件与材料都齐全，所以不存在“连接件本来做不完”的问题。
陈未将连接件板移到墙边并启动标牌文件时，资源用途已经确定。
连接件对周一实物卡合确认有明确价值，因此是被放弃的最佳可行替代，而不是无关紧要的备用项目。
周一确认推迟只是把这项价值显出来；机会成本在周五选择时已经产生。
mapping: 最后九十分钟 → 稀缺但没有现金价格的设备容量。
二十四块触觉标牌 → 被选择的资源用途。
六个展架连接件 → 同时可行且有真实价值的最佳替代。
周一缺少实物卡合确认 → 被放弃替代价值的后续表现。
“连接件—周三”透明板 → 替代用途后来仍可完成，但周五那次机会已过去。
moduleZh.boundary: 机会成本不是按截止日期排序的同义词，也不是所有未完成项目的总和。即使所选方案合理，仍可能有机会成本；关键是选择当时是否存在一个真实可行且有价值的最佳替代。本故事中的创客室、人物和项目均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么陈未先做标牌可以是一个合理决定，同时仍意味着她放弃了周一实物连接件所具有的机会价值？

references.citation: Buchanan, James M. *Cost and Choice: An Inquiry in Economic Theory*. 1969. Liberty Fund edition, 1999.
references.use: Used to support the idea that cost is tied to choice, that opportunity cost depends on the opportunity displaced by the chosen action, and that it can involve subjective value rather than cash expenditure alone.

references.citation: Greenlaw, Steven A., David Shapiro, and Daniel MacDonald. “How Individuals Make Choices Based on Their Budget Constraint.” *Principles of Economics 3e*. OpenStax, 2022.
references.use: Used to support opportunity cost as the value of the next-best feasible alternative forgone, including scarce non-cash resources such as time.

referencesZh.citation: Buchanan, James M. *Cost and Choice: An Inquiry in Economic Theory*. 1969. Liberty Fund edition, 1999.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持成本与选择相联系、机会成本取决于被选择行为所排开的机会，并包含主观价值而不只现金支出的理解。

referencesZh.citation: Greenlaw, Steven A., David Shapiro, and Daniel MacDonald. “How Individuals Make Choices Based on Their Budget Constraint.” *Principles of Economics 3e*. OpenStax, 2022.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持机会成本是放弃的下一最佳可行替代方案的价值，并可包含时间等非现金稀缺资源。

articles.title: The Last Oven Slot Before Noon
articles.summary: Before noon, Xu Yan receives two requests for ten extra lunches: one needs them on time, the other can collect forty minutes later. One empty oven slot and an unconfirmed café order remain.
storyParagraphs: At 11:20, Xu Yan has already divided fifty lunch boxes into five stacks and finished the labels. The kitchen rent for the day, €120, was paid that morning, and the original orders are priced at €12 per meal. Only one oven slot remains before noon. The café next door had asked earlier about adding a tray of brownies; if Xu Yan confirms by 11:30, the order will go ahead and leave a €20 net contribution. She has not committed to it yet.

The design company upstairs messages: could it add ten lunches at €10 each for collection at noon? The refrigerator still holds unopened ingredients reserved for later orders, and a pack of boxes remains. Using them today would require replacing €45 of ingredients and €10 of packaging at normal purchase prices. The meals would also take the last oven slot before noon. Xu Yan puts the café’s note beside the new order.

On the slip, she writes the resources this batch would use: €45 of food, €10 of packaging, and €20 for another half hour of help. Accepting the lunches would also forgo the still-available brownie add-on’s €20 net contribution. The ten meals bring in €100: 100 − (45 + 10 + 20 + 20) = +5. Before 11:30, she clips the design company’s slip onto the order board and tells the café she has no spare oven slot today.

Twelve minutes later, a nearby studio asks for another ten lunches at the same €10 each, but says it can collect them at 12:40. Once the noon batch leaves, the oven will have another free slot, so equipment time is available. The problem is different now: the regular food stock is exhausted. A nearby supplier can rush over another batch, but charges €30 for the delivery, and the helper would need to stay for a second extra half hour.

Xu Yan writes a fresh note: €45 for food, €10 for packaging, €20 for the second extra half hour of help, and €30 for urgent delivery—€105 in all, against €100 in revenue. Her helper has set the next pack of boxes on the counter and is waiting for an answer. Xu Yan slides the note beside her phone and replies, “I can’t do it at that price today. Confirm the numbers tomorrow, and I’ll quote again with normal preparation.” The studio says it will send the headcount that afternoon.

By noon, the original fifty meals have been sent out and the design company has collected its ten additional boxes. The helper washes the newly emptied tray and stands it on the drying rack; the café’s brownie note goes into the folder for unconfirmed add-ons. Xu Yan returns her phone to its charging stand. Beside it, the note still reads “100 − 105 = −5,” and the next pack of boxes remains unopened.
articles.overall: Marginal analysis compares the added benefit and cost of the next step from the current position. Already-paid costs stay fixed; a still-available benefit forgone because of the decision counts as opportunity cost. Changed conditions require a fresh comparison.
explanationParagraphs: The first batch earns €100, consumes ingredients and packaging worth €45 and €10 to replace for later orders, adds €20 of labor, and forgoes the available €20 brownie contribution: a net gain of €5. The stock retains usable value; the calculation concerns extra consumption and replacement, not charging its past purchase twice.

The second offer allows collection at 12:40. Accepting it would use a new oven slot but add €45+€10+€20+€30=€105 in costs against €100 revenue, a net reduction of €5, so Xu Yan declines. Paid rent and the already-lost brownie opportunity stay unchanged.

module.intro: The same request for “ten more” can produce a different decision once current capacity, pickup time, and still-available alternatives have changed.
module.diagramTitle: Why the Two Ten-Meal Add-ons Lead to Different Decisions
diagramSteps: Hold the confirmed fifty meals and already-paid costs fixed
Identify the oven slot and feasible add-on displaced by the first batch
Calculate the first batch’s extra benefit and extra cost
After accepting the first batch, update committed resources and the next available slot
Calculate the second batch using only the new conditions
diagramStepNotes: The €120 kitchen rent has already been paid and does not change with either add-on.
The first batch uses the last oven slot before noon and gives up a still-confirmable €20 brownie net contribution.
Food/packaging could serve later orders and would cost €45/€10 to replace; 100 − (45 + 10 + 20 + 20) = +5.
At the second inquiry, a post-noon slot would be available for a later pickup; the accepted first batch has committed the remaining regular food stock.
mapping: Unconfirmed café brownie note → a real alternative still available when the first decision is made.
Design company slip clipped to the order board → the first marginal comparison changes behavior.
12:40 pickup → the second batch has a new oven slot.
€30 urgent delivery fee → a new cost that exists only for the second batch.
module.boundary: Opportunity cost must be a genuine alternative available at the moment of decision; the same lost or already-realized item cannot be counted again later. Marginal analysis compares the current next step. If pickup time, capacity, price, or alternatives change, the relevant conditions must be updated and recalculated.
module.reflection: When the first add-on has already changed the available oven time and alternatives, which conditions would you update first when a second add-on arrives so that old and new costs are not mixed together?

references.citation: Greenlaw, S. A., Shapiro, D., & MacDonald, D. (2022). Principles of Economics 3e, §2.1: How Individuals Make Choices Based on Their Budget Constraint. OpenStax.
references.use: Supports the modern teaching definitions of incremental benefits, incremental costs, and opportunity cost; it is not used as a single historical origin for marginal analysis.
