articles.titleZh: 十二点前的最后一个烤盘
articles.summaryZh: 十二点前，许妍收到两个追加十份的询价：一个要准时取，一个能晚四十分钟。台面上只剩一个空烤盘和咖啡店等待确认的便签。
storyParagraphsZh: 十一点二十，许妍已经把五十份午餐盒分成五摞，标签也贴完了。当天厨房租金120欧元早上已经刷卡，原订单每份12欧元。烤架上只剩十二点前最后一个空档。隔壁咖啡店上午问过一盘布朗尼，若她十一点半前确认就能成交，做完可留下20欧元净贡献；现在还没承诺。
这时楼上设计公司发来消息：能不能临时加十份午餐，每份10欧元，十二点取走。冷藏柜里还有留给后续订单的未开封食材，纸盒也剩一包；若今天用掉，就要按正常进货价补回食材45欧元、包装10欧元。十份午餐还会占掉十二点前最后一个烤盘时段。许妍把咖啡店的便签和新订单并排放在台面上。
她在订单背面写下这批会多用的资源：食材45欧元、包装10欧元，帮工多留半小时20欧元。若接午餐，布朗尼这个仍可确认的加单就得放弃，再计20欧元净贡献。十份午餐收入100欧元，100－(45＋10＋20＋20)＝＋5。十一点半前，她把设计公司的纸签夹进订单板，回复咖啡店今天没有多余烤盘时段。
十二分钟后，附近工作室又问能否加十份，仍是每份10欧元，但可以十二点四十分再来取。十二点那批出完后，烤箱会重新空出一个时段，所以设备时间够用；问题变成常规食材已经用完。附近供应商可以加急补一批，送货费30欧元，帮工还要再多留半小时。
许妍重新写一张便签：食材45、包装10、第二段额外人工20、加急补货30，共105欧元；这批收入还是100欧元。帮工已经把下一包纸盒放到台面，等她回复。许妍将便签推到手机旁，给工作室回了一句：“今天这个价格做不了，明天先确认人数，再按正常备料重新报价。”对方回说，下午把人数发来。
到十二点，原来的五十份午餐陆续送出，设计公司也取走了追加的十份。帮工洗净刚腾空的烤盘，立在沥水架上；咖啡店的布朗尼便签被收进未确认加单夹。许妍把手机放回充电座，旁边那张便签上留着“100－105＝－5”，新的一包纸盒还没拆开。
articles.overallZh: 边际分析比较当前选择下一小步的新增收益与新增成本。已经付出的费用保持不变，仍可选择却因本次决定被放弃的收益计入机会成本；条件变了，计算也要重做。
explanationParagraphsZh: 第一批收入100欧元，消耗可留作后续订单、补回价值45与10欧元的食材和包装，另加人工20，并放弃尚可确认的布朗尼净贡献20，净增5。存货有继续使用价值，计的是新增消耗及补货，不是重复计已付货款。
第二个询价允许十二点四十分取货：若接下，可用新烤箱时段，但会新增45＋10＋20＋30＝105欧元成本，对100欧元收入净减5欧元，因此被拒。已付租金和已失去的布朗尼机会保持不变。

moduleZh.intro: 同样是“再加十份”，只要当前容量、取货时间和仍可选择的机会变了，增量比较就要重新做。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 两个追加单为何得到不同决定
diagramSteps: 固定已确认五十份与已支付费用
识别第一批会占用的时段与可行加单
计算第一批新增收益和新增代价
接受第一批后，更新已用资源与下一个可用时段
只按新条件计算第二批十份
diagramStepNotes: 120欧元厨房租金已经支付，不随追加单改变。
第一批占用十二点前最后烤盘，放弃尚可确认的20欧元布朗尼净贡献。
在第二次询价时，十二点后的新空档可供晚取订单使用；已接的第一批占去常规食材余量。
mapping: 咖啡店未确认的布朗尼便签 → 第一批决策时仍可选择的机会。
设计公司纸签进入订单板 → 第一次比较后实际接单。
十二点四十分取货 → 第二批拥有新的烤箱时段。
30欧元加急补货费 → 第二批才出现的新增成本。
moduleZh.boundary: 机会成本必须是决策当时真实可行的替代机会，不能把已经失去或已经发生的同一项再次计算。边际分析比较当前一步的变化；若取货时间、容量、价格或替代机会改变，就需要更新条件重新计算。
moduleZh.reflection: 当第一笔追加已经改变了可用时段和替代机会，第二笔追加到来时，你会先更新哪些条件，才能避免把旧成本和新成本混在一起？

referencesZh.citation: Greenlaw, S. A., Shapiro, D., & MacDonald, D. (2022). Principles of Economics 3e, §2.1: How Individuals Make Choices Based on Their Budget Constraint. OpenStax.
referencesZh.use: 支持增量收益、增量成本与机会成本的现代教学定义；不作为边际分析的单一历史起源。

referencesZh.citation: Greenlaw, S. A., Shapiro, D., & MacDonald, D. (2022). Principles of Economics 3e, §7.2: Production in the Short Run. OpenStax.
referencesZh.use: 支持短期固定投入约束与新增投入、产出之间的区分；故事数值与场景均为原创假设。

articles.title: The Third Morning in the Courtyard
articles.titleZh: 院子里多出来的第三个早晨
articles.summary: Tang Jing moves her morning movement class into a free courtyard approved for community use. She halves the price, fills two sessions, and adds Friday—just as a night-shift interpreter upstairs begins changing his own schedule.
articles.summaryZh: 唐静把晨间律动课搬进获准使用的免费院子，价格减半，两场很快满员。她加开周五时，三楼一名从未报名的夜班口译员也开始改自己的时间表。
storyParagraphs: At 8:00 on Monday morning, Tang Jing taught her first morning movement class in the courtyard shared by the residential building and community center. The property manager had already allowed residents and community programs to book the courtyard during the day. Tang Jing had previously rented a small indoor room by the hour; now she reduced the price per class from €12 to €6. The Monday and Wednesday sessions filled quickly, the waiting list kept growing, and she agreed to add a Friday morning class the following week.

On the third floor, Zhou Ning worked remote overnight shifts as a medical interpreter, starting before dawn and finishing at 9:00, often with one final call at 8:30. He had not enrolled in the class and did not know most of the participants. During the first two mornings, he could finish his shift by closing the windows and wearing noise-cancelling headphones. When the Friday session was added, the drums and the footsteps of more than twenty people again fell into the same working hour. At 8:10, he closed his laptop, packed his bag, and went to a coworking space around the corner.

A sound-insulated booth there cost €12. The following Wednesday and Friday, he did not wait for the noise to start; he booked the same booth in advance, left home at 7:50, and moved the final hour of his existing night shift there. Tang Jing, meanwhile, still had a waiting list for all three classes. The €6 price covered the costs she could see—her time and speaker batteries—and the courtyard carried no rent. She even began asking whether a Thursday session could be added.

At the end of the month, the coworking space combined Zhou Ning’s three bookings into one €36 bill. He did not ask for the classes to stop. He sent the bill, his night-shift schedule, and a note asking whether they could find a way to coexist to the property manager. The manager forwarded the email to Tang Jing. When she opened the attachment, her own course sheet still said “courtyard rent: €0,” beside three full class lists. The €36 was not a total of every neighbor’s loss, but it was one third-party expense that had been completely absent from her accounts.

They first tried the option that changed the class schedule least. The next Monday, every participant wore headphones, Tang Jing stopped broadcasting spoken instructions, and the stepping area was moved toward the center of the courtyard. Zhou Ning stayed home and continued his normal night shift. The sound was much lower, but the dull thud of more than twenty people landing at once still reached his 8:30 call. That afternoon, Tang Jing booked the Wednesday and Friday classes back into the small indoor room and left Monday in the courtyard.

When the new schedule went up, Monday still read “Courtyard 08:00,” while Wednesday and Friday now said “Small room.” The two indoor sessions were raised to €9, and the waiting list became shorter. Zhou Ning cancelled two coworking bookings for the following week. Tang Jing added a new line to her fee sheet—“indoor room rent”—with a printed copy of the €36 bill clipped beside it.
storyParagraphsZh: 周一早上八点，唐静在住宅与社区中心共用的内院上第一节晨间律动课。物业已经允许住户和社区项目在白天预约院子；她原来租室内小厅，每小时要付场地费，现在把单次价格从十二欧降到六欧。周一、周三两场很快满员，候补名单还在增长，她答应下周再加一个周五早晨。
三楼的周宁做远程夜班医疗口译，凌晨开始，早上九点结束，八点半往往还有最后一段连线。他没有报名课程，也不认识大多数学生。头两个早晨，他关窗、戴降噪耳机还能把班上完；周五第三场第一次出现时，鼓点和二十多人的踏步又落在同一工作时段，他在八点十分合上电脑，背包去了街角的共享办公室。
那天的隔音工位十二欧。下一周三、周五，他不再等声音起来才决定，而是提前订了同一个位置，七点五十分出门，把本来就存在的夜班最后一小时搬到那里。唐静这边，三场都有人候补，六欧仍能覆盖她看得见的时间和音响电池成本；院子没有租金，她甚至开始询问周四是否还能增加一场。
月底，共享办公室把三次预约合成一张36欧账单。周宁没有要求停课，只把账单、自己的夜班排班和一句“能不能找个共存办法”一起发给物业。管理员随后把邮件转给唐静。她打开附件时，自己的课程表正写着“院子租金：0”，旁边是三场满员名单。36欧不是所有邻居损失的总数，却是她此前账目里完全看不到的一笔第三方支出。
他们先试了最少改变课程的办法。下一周周一，学员全部改戴耳机，唐静不再外放口令，踏步区也缩到院子中间。周宁留在家里继续原来的夜班；声音少了许多，可二十多个人同时落脚的闷响仍会进入八点半的通话。当天午后，唐静把周三、周五两场订回室内小厅，周一继续留在院子。
新课表贴出时，周一仍写“院子 08:00”，周三、周五后面改成“小厅”，室内两场价格调到九欧，候补名单短了一截。周宁取消下一周两次共享办公室预约。唐静在收费表上新增“室内厅租金”一行，旁边夹着那张36欧账单打印件。
explanationParagraphs: A negative externality occurs when part of the cost of an activity falls on a third party outside the transaction and is not fully included in the private price facing the decision-maker. Lower private cost can support a lower price or a higher level of activity.

Harm alone does not automatically make something an externality. The key is that the affected third party did not take part in the transaction; one bill can also show only part of a visible burden, not precisely measure the full social cost.
explanationParagraphsZh: 负外部性指一项活动把部分成本落在交易之外的第三方身上，而这部分成本没有充分进入决策者面对的私人价格。较低的私人成本可能支持更低价格或更多活动。
有损害并不自动构成外部性。关键是第三方未参与相关交易；某张账单也只能显示一部分可见成本，不等于精确计算全部社会成本。
articles.overall: The courtyard class is permitted, popular, and not malicious. Zhou Ning can still work from home during the first two sessions, but once the third session is added, the repeated disturbance conflicts persistently with his existing night-shift schedule and he begins paying for sound-insulated booths on class days. Three €12 bookings produce a €36 bill that makes one third-party cost visible, not the full social cost. Once part of that cost enters Tang Jing’s decisions, the venue, price, and number of courtyard sessions change.
articles.overallZh: 院子课得到允许、受欢迎且没有恶意。前两场时周宁尚能在家工作，第三场加入后，重复频率与既有夜班时段发生持续冲突，他才开始在课程日支付隔音工位费用。三次12欧形成的36欧账单只是一个可见的第三方成本，不是全部社会成本；当部分成本进入唐静的安排后，场地、价格和场次数量随之调整。

module.intro: The courtyard is approved for use, and Zhou Ning can still finish his night shift during the first two classes. A third session spreads the same effect across three mornings, leading him to buy sound-insulated workspace for an existing job—a cost absent from the class price.
module.diagramTitle: How a third-party cost can remain outside the private price
diagramSteps: A permitted activity creates private benefits for the people in the transaction
As activity frequency rises, a third party outside the transaction bears a recurring cost
The third party pays for mitigation in order to maintain an existing activity
That expense was not originally included in the producer’s private price
Once part of the outside cost becomes visible, private arrangements and activity levels adjust
diagramStepNotes: The property manager allows use of the courtyard, so the story does not depend on an obvious rule violation.
Zhou Ning can work from home during the first two sessions and changes location only after the third morning is added, tying the problem to repeated activity level.
The coworking booth is a way to continue his existing night-shift interpreting work, not a complaint from someone who bought the class.
Three €12 bookings create a €36 bill that makes one external burden visible, but it cannot stand for every neighbor’s cost or the full social cost.
Headphones reduce only part of the impact; moving two sessions indoors is one adjustment in this story, not a universally necessary solution.
mapping: Permitted free courtyard use and a €6 class price → lower private cost and price.
The third morning → greater activity frequency crosses what Zhou Ning can manage within his existing work arrangement.
Three sound-insulated booth bookings → mitigation costs borne by a third party outside the transaction.
The €36 bill beside “courtyard rent: €0” → the private account does not include every cost generated by the activity.
The headphone trial and two sessions moving indoors → different mitigation methods can change costs and activity arrangements without implying one inevitable solution.
module.boundary: A negative externality does not require malicious or illegal behavior, and not every neighborhood inconvenience is a social cost. What matters is whether a cost falls on a third party outside the transaction and is not fully included in private decision-making. One person’s bill cannot fully measure an external cost; negotiation, technology, rules, charges, or venue changes may all be partial responses. The courtyard, characters, and classes in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why are Zhou Ning’s three coworking expenses connected to the classes, while the €36 still cannot simply be treated as the entire social cost caused by the morning sessions?

moduleZh.intro: 院子获准使用，前两场课也尚未妨碍周宁完成夜班。第三场把同一种影响扩展到三个早晨，他为了保住原有工作时段开始购买隔音工位；这笔费用从未出现在课程票价里。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 第三方成本怎样留在私人价格之外
diagramSteps: 合法活动为交易双方创造私人收益
活动频率增加后给交易外第三方带来持续成本
第三方为维持既有活动自行承担缓解支出
这些支出原先没有进入生产者面对的私人价格
部分成本被看见后，私人安排和活动水平发生调整
diagramStepNotes: 物业允许院子使用，因此故事不依赖明显违规这一解释。
周宁前两场能在家完成工作，第三场加入后才开始改变工作地点，显示问题与重复活动水平相关。
共享办公室是为了继续完成既有夜班口译，不是因为他购买课程后对服务不满意。
三次12欧形成36欧账单，使一项具体外部负担可见，但不能代表所有邻居成本或全部社会成本。
耳机只能减少一部分影响；两场搬回小厅是这个故事中的一种调整，而不是普遍唯一方案。
mapping: 获准使用的免费院子与六欧票价 → 较低的私人成本和价格。
第三个早晨 → 活动频率提高并越过周宁原有工作的可承受安排。
三次隔音工位预约 → 交易外第三方为维持既有工作承担的缓解成本。
36欧账单与“院子租金：0”并置 → 私人账目没有包含全部由活动引出的成本。
耳机试课及两场回到小厅 → 不同缓解方式会改变成本与活动安排，但没有单一必然方案。
moduleZh.boundary: 负外部性不等于生产者恶意、违规，也不等于任何邻里不便都是社会成本。关键是相关成本是否落在交易之外的第三方且未充分进入私人决策。外部成本难以由一张个人账单完整计量，协商、技术、规则、收费或场地调整都可能是部分回应。本故事中的院子、人物与课程均为虚构。

articles.title: Six Names for Wednesday Morning
articles.titleZh: 星期三早上的六个名字
articles.summary: The car-free period outside a school needs six parents to volunteer for twenty minutes each day. Xu Cheng receives more than a dozen offers to help, yet by Tuesday night Wednesday's sixth box still holds only two pencilled question marks.
articles.summaryZh: 校门前的无车时段每天需要六名家长轮值二十分钟。许澄收到十几条愿意帮忙的私信，可到周二晚上，周三表格的第六格仍只有两个铅笔问号。
storyParagraphs: At 7:45 on Monday morning, Qinghe Elementary School began its first twenty-minute car-free arrival period. The community center had delivered two sets of movable barriers to the school entrance, but the rule was that at least six registered volunteers had to each cover twenty minutes before both ends of the street could be temporarily closed. Parent Xu Cheng was responsible for organizing the following week’s roster. By lunchtime, Wednesday had only three names; the fourth, fifth, and sixth boxes were still blank.

Private messages kept arriving that afternoon. One parent had an 8:00 meeting and said, “Call me if you already have five.” Another could do either Wednesday or Friday but wanted to wait and see which day needed help more. A third genuinely could not volunteer that week but still hoped to use the car-free street every morning when dropping off a child. Once the street was closed, families that had not signed up benefited too. Xu Cheng wrote the conditions in the margins, but the formal roster still stopped at three names.

By Tuesday evening, Wednesday had finally reached five. Beside the sixth box, Xu Cheng penciled two question marks: two parents had both said, “If you really need me, I’ll come,” but neither wanted to lock in twenty minutes before knowing whether the others would show up. At 7:45 the next morning, all five confirmed volunteers were there and the sixth box was still empty. The community worker did not lift out the barriers, and several drop-off cars continued to pass in front of the gate.

After school, Xu Cheng spread the paper roster and more than a dozen conditional messages across a bench. She did not blame any particular absent parent. Instead, she changed the following week’s form so that conditional commitments themselves were visible: a parent could first mark “available,” and the page would show how many people were already available for that day. Once six were reached, all six would receive a confirmation request. If fewer than six remained by 8:00 p.m., families would be notified in advance that the street would not close the next morning; confirmed volunteers could swap with another registered parent if necessary.

The new form still had blank spaces on its first evening. Four people first marked themselves available for Wednesday; a fifth joined after seeing the count, and a sixth later confirmed. The paper sign-in sheet eventually showed six names, with one swap arrow beside them. Monday, however, still had only four confirmed volunteers, so the community announced the night before that it would not close. On the other four car-free days, families that had not volunteered used the same twenty-minute car-free street as the families that had.

At the end of the second week, Xu Cheng clipped the two weeks’ rosters together. The sixth Wednesday box on the first sheet still carried a penciled question mark; the same box on the second sheet now held a signature. Monday still had two empty boxes. The barriers by the gate were pushed back into the community storeroom, and next week’s dates were left at the bottom of the roster.
storyParagraphsZh: 周一早上七点四十五，青禾小学门口第一次试行二十分钟无车接送。社区中心把两组可移动路障送到校门边，却规定每天至少六名登记志愿者各守二十分钟，才能把两端临时封住。家长许澄负责排下周轮值。到午饭前，周三那一栏只有三个名字，第四、第五、第六格都还是空的。
下午私信却不断跳出来。有人八点要开会，说“如果已经有五个就叫我”；有人周三和周五都能来，但想先看看哪天更缺；还有人这周确实无法轮值，却仍希望每天送孩子时能走无车路。因为路一旦封住，没报名的家庭也一样受益。许澄把条件写在纸表边上，正式名字仍停在三个。
到周二晚上，周三栏终于写到五个人。第六格旁边，许澄铅笔写了两个问号，因为两位家长都说“真缺我就来”，却都不愿在不知道别人是否到场时先锁死自己的二十分钟。第二天七点四十五，五个人准时站在校门口，第六格仍空着。社区工作人员没有抬出路障，几辆送学车照常穿过门前。
放学后，许澄把纸表和十几条条件式私信摊在长椅上。她没有把问题归到某个没来的家长身上，而是把下周表格改成让条件承诺本身可见：名字旁可以先标“可来”，页面实时显示已有几人；某天累计到六个可来者后，再同时发确认。晚上八点前仍不足六人，就提前通知第二天不封路；确认后临时有事，可和另一名已登记家长交换。
新的表格第一晚仍有空格。周三四个人先标“可来”，第五个人看到人数后补上，第六个人随后确认；纸质签到表上最终有六个名字，旁边还画了一次换班箭头。可星期一仍只有四人，社区前一晚就通知不封路。其余四个封路日里，没有轮值的家庭仍和轮值家庭一样使用那二十分钟无车路。
第二周结束，许澄把两周表格一起夹进文件夹。第一张周三栏第六格还留着铅笔问号，第二张同一位置已经签了名字；星期一那一栏仍空着两格。门边的路障被推回社区仓库，名单最下面留着下周日期。
explanationParagraphs: A collective action problem arises when a shared outcome requires enough people to contribute, while its benefits are difficult to reserve only for contributors. Everyone may genuinely value the outcome and still have reason to wait for others to bear the time, money, or risk first.

Communication, monitoring, conditional commitments, and rules can reduce uncertainty, but they do not remove the structure in which noncontributors can still benefit. Better cooperation does not mean the problem has permanently disappeared.
explanationParagraphsZh: 集体行动困境出现在共享结果需要足够多人贡献，而收益又难以只留给贡献者时。每个人都可能真心重视结果，却仍有理由等待别人先承担时间、金钱或风险。
沟通、监测、条件承诺和规则能降低不确定性，但不能消除“不贡献也可受益”的结构，因此合作改善不等于困境永久解决。
articles.overall: Six parents must each give twenty minutes to create a car-free street that every family can then use; families that do not volunteer are not excluded from the benefit. That makes “call me when you already have five” individually understandable, yet many such decisions can leave the sixth box empty. The new form mainly changes what commitments people can see and reduces uncertainty. It does not remove free access to the benefit, which is why Monday still has only four volunteers in the second week.
articles.overallZh: 每天六名家长各付出二十分钟，才能形成所有家庭都可使用的无车路；未轮值者并不会被排除在收益之外。因此“差一个再叫我”对单个人有现实理由，却可能让第六格一直空着。新表格主要改变了大家能看见的承诺和不确定性，没有改变免费受益的结构，所以第二周仍有一天只有四人。

module.intro: Once six parents each give twenty minutes, every family can use the car-free street, including families that did not volunteer. The old form makes coordination harder, but clearer information does not remove the gap between who contributes and who benefits.
module.diagramTitle: How shared benefits and a contribution threshold create a collective action problem
diagramSteps: A shared outcome requires individuals to bear a real contribution cost
Once the threshold is reached, contributors and noncontributors share the benefit
When others’ participation is uncertain, waiting can be individually reasonable
If many people wait at once, the contribution threshold can fail
Visible commitments reduce uncertainty but do not eliminate the free-rider structure
diagramStepNotes: Each volunteer must actually give twenty minutes, so contributing is not costless.
Once the car-free period is created, families that did not volunteer can still use it, so the benefit cannot be reserved for the six contributors.
“Call me when you already have five” reduces the risk of showing up unnecessarily or bearing the burden alone, so it is not evidence of indifference.
Five volunteers genuinely arrive in the first week and still cannot close the street, showing how individually reasonable waiting can add up to collective failure.
The second-week form improves information and commitments, but Monday still has only four volunteers, showing that a better interface does not remove the basic incentive structure.
mapping: Twenty minutes of volunteer duty per person → a real individual contribution cost.
The six-person threshold → the minimum contribution required for the shared outcome.
Nonvolunteering families still use the car-free street → the benefit cannot be limited to contributors.
The question mark in Wednesday’s sixth box → conditional waiting caused by uncertainty about others’ participation.
Two blank boxes on Monday in the second week → the collective action problem can recur even after coordination improves.
module.boundary: A collective action problem does not show that participants are selfish, foolish, or unconcerned about the shared outcome, and not every scheduling problem is a collective action problem. Here, shared benefits, a real personal contribution cost, and uncertainty about others’ actions all coexist. Communication, monitoring, commitments, and rules can improve cooperation, but their effects depend on the setting. The school, community, and families in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why can making conditional commitments visible help Wednesday reach six volunteers without guaranteeing that Monday will also succeed?

moduleZh.intro: 每天六名家长各付出二十分钟后，所有家庭都能使用无车路，包括没有轮值的人。旧表格加重了协调困难，但即使信息更清楚，贡献成本与共享收益之间的差别仍然存在。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 共享收益与贡献门槛怎样形成集体行动困境
diagramSteps: 共同结果需要个人承担真实贡献成本
达到门槛后收益向贡献者和未贡献者共同开放
他人是否参与不确定时，等待具有个人合理性
多人同时等待会让贡献门槛落空
可见承诺降低不确定性，但不消除搭便车结构
diagramStepNotes: 每名志愿者需要实际承担二十分钟轮值，因此贡献并非零成本。
无车路形成后，没有轮值的家庭仍可使用，收益无法只留给六名志愿者。
“已有五个再叫我”能减少个人白跑或单独承担的风险，所以并非冷漠。
第一周五人真实到场仍无法封路，显示局部合理等待可以叠加成集体失败。
第二周表格改善了信息和承诺，但星期一仍只有四人，说明界面改进没有消除基本激励结构。
mapping: 每人二十分钟轮值 → 真实的个人贡献成本。
六人门槛 → 共享结果必须达到的最低贡献量。
未轮值家庭照样走无车路 → 收益不能只留给贡献者。
周三第六格的问号 → 对他人行动不确定导致的条件式等待。
第二周星期一仍空两格 → 协调改善后，集体行动困境仍可能再次出现。
moduleZh.boundary: 集体行动困境不说明参与者自私、愚蠢或不重视共同结果，也不等于所有排班问题都是集体行动问题。这里的关键是共享收益、真实个人贡献成本与他人行动不确定性同时存在。沟通、监测、承诺和规则可能改善合作，但效果依情境而异。本故事中的学校、社区与家庭均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么让条件承诺变得可见能帮助周三凑够六人，却不能保证星期一也一定成功？

articles.title: The Permit at 4:20
articles.titleZh: 十六点二十分的通行证
articles.summary: At 16:20 on Saturday, the municipal plaza lowers its vehicle barrier early, leaving Lin Su’s three hundred festival programs outside. Her permit is valid until 17:00, the information desk is waiting to pack the programs, and plaza management is dealing with a sudden surge in foot traffic.
articles.summaryZh: 周六16:20，市政广场的车辆栏杆提前落下，林素订好的三百份节目单被挡在外面。通行证写着17:00前有效，信息台已经等着装袋，而管理处正忙着应付突然增大的人流。
storyParagraphs: At 16:20 on Saturday, Lin Su stood at the east entrance to the municipal plaza, with three hundred festival programs still in the delivery van. Her permit said “delivery valid before 17:00,” but the east barrier was already down. Eight volunteers at the information desk were supposed to start packing audience bags at 16:30. The driver checked the map: going around to the underground loading entrance would add at least forty minutes.

The plaza manager came out of the booth and explained that foot traffic had grown unexpectedly, so vehicles had been stopped at 16:00. He showed Lin Su the operating manual, which did allow staff to “adjust entrances and guidance according to on-site conditions.” Lin Su asked whether that also meant changing 17:00 to 16:00. The manager did not take away her permit; he only said that crowd control had to come first. The delivery company had already started charging waiting time.

Lin Su called the review number printed on the back of the permit. After checking the permit number, the duty officer added the plaza manager to the same call. The dispute was logged with the municipal rules review office, and plaza management could not withdraw the case and handle it internally. The reviewer did not ask how the barrier should be positioned; they pulled up the existing rule and operating manual and checked only whether the current text authorized a change to the cutoff time. The boxes of programs stayed untouched in the van, the driver switched off the engine, and the waiting fee kept rising.

A little over ten minutes later, the review office gave a narrow decision: the 17:00 cutoff still stood. Plaza management could redirect vehicles, narrow the lane, or admit vans one at a time, but it could not treat “adjusting entrances” as authority to move the vehicle ban forward by an hour. The reviewer also could not create a new 16:00 rule or tell staff how to operate the barrier. The manager looked at the growing crowd and decided to move the barrier just far enough for one vehicle to pass. The delivery van entered at 16:48.

By the time the programs reached the information desk, the volunteer briefing had lost more than twenty minutes, and the delivery company had added a waiting charge. When the first visitors arrived, one unopened stack of programs was still sitting on the corner of the table. Management did not remove its other crowd measures; instead, it made the opposite entrance one-way and stationed staff to guide people on foot. Later, the manager added “weekend vehicle ban from 16:00” to the agenda for the following week’s council meeting.

At exactly 17:00, the east barrier came down again. Lin Su slipped the permit back into the delivery folder. Its time stamp read “16:48.” Outside the barrier, the next vehicle without a permit had already turned around, while the information desk was finally opening the last stack of programs.
storyParagraphsZh: 周六下午四点二十分，林素站在市政广场东口，三百份音乐节节目单就在配送车后厢里。她手里的通行证写着“17:00前配送有效”，东口栏杆却已经放下。信息台八名志愿者原定四点半开始装观众袋；司机看了导航，若绕地下卸货口，至少多四十分钟。
管理处主管从岗亭出来，解释下午人流突然变大，所以十六点就把车辆挡在外面。他翻出执行手册，上面确实允许“根据现场情况调整入口和引导方式”。林素问这是否也包括把十七点改成十六点。主管没有收走通行证，只说现场秩序得先处理；等待计费已经开始。
林素拨通通行证背面的复核电话。值班员核对证号后，把管理处主管也接进同一通话；这项争议登记在市政规则复核室，管理处不能把工单撤回本处处理。复核员没有问该怎样摆栏杆，只调出既有规则和执行手册，确认现行文本有没有授权改变禁入时限。后厢里的节目单仍一箱没动，司机关掉发动机，等待费继续往上跳。
十几分钟后，复核室给出很窄的结论：十七点时限仍有效；管理处可以改入口、缩窄通道、逐辆放行，却不能把“调整入口”直接当成提前一小时禁车。复核员也不能自己制定一个十六点新规则，更不会指挥现场怎么开栏杆。主管看了一眼不断进场的人群，决定只移开够一辆车通过的宽度。配送车在十六点四十八分驶入。
节目单送到信息台时，培训已经少了二十多分钟，配送公司也多记了一段等待费。第一批观众进场时，桌角还有一摞节目单没拆封。管理处没有撤掉其他人流措施，反而把另一侧入口改成单向，并安排人员步行引导。晚些时候，主管把“周末十六点起禁车”的建议写进下周议事会议程。
十七点整，东口栏杆再次合上。林素把通行证夹回配送文件袋，上面的时间章是“16:48”。栏杆外，下一辆没有通行证的车已经调头，信息台那边终于把最后一摞节目单拆开。
explanationParagraphs: Separation of powers assigns general rule-making, rule execution, and final dispute resolution to functions with real independence, so an executor cannot turn its own interpretation into both a new rule and the final judgment.
Separation does not mean complete isolation. Executive bodies still need room to act, while reviewing bodies should not take over rule-making or execution.
explanationParagraphsZh: 权力分立把制定一般规则、执行规则和最终裁决争议交给具有实际独立性的不同职能，使执行者不能把自己的解释同时变成新规则和终局判决。
分立不等于彼此隔绝。执行机关仍需有行动空间；裁决机关也不能越俎代庖制定规则或代替执行。
articles.overall: The existing rule sets the 17:00 cutoff, plaza management handles on-site execution, and the independent review office decides only whether management’s interpretation exceeds its authority. The review office cannot create a new 16:00 rule in place of the rule-making body or operate the barrier for management; management still keeps discretion over one-way routing, lane width, and admitting vehicles one at a time. The waiting charge, lost training time, and unopened programs make the friction of institutional checks visible, without implying that every administrative delay is caused by divided power.
articles.overallZh: 十七点时限由既有规则确定，管理处负责现场执行，独立复核室只判断执行解释是否越过授权。它既不能替议事机构制定十六点新规则，也不替管理处摆栏杆；管理处仍保留改单向、缩通道和逐辆放行的执行空间。等待费、培训损失和未拆节目单显示了制度摩擦的现实成本，但故事不把所有行政延迟都归因于分权。

module.intro: A general rule first marks the boundary of executive authority. The executing body then responds to conditions on the ground, while an independent reviewing body decides only whether the interpretation exceeds that authority. Each function constrains the others while retaining room to do its own work.
module.diagramTitle: How rule-making, execution, and review constrain one another
diagramSteps: A general rule first sets the public boundary of executive authority
The executing body acts in response to conditions on the ground
A dispute arises between the executive interpretation and the existing rule
An independent reviewing body decides only whether the interpretation exceeds its authority
If the general rule needs to change, the issue returns to the rule-making process
diagramStepNotes: The 17:00 cutoff is already written on the permit, so plaza management cannot rewrite it that day through its own interpretation alone.
Management can still narrow the lane, make an entrance one-way, and admit vehicles individually, showing that separation does not eliminate executive capacity.
The review case cannot be withdrawn by plaza management or turned into an internal reconsideration, which gives the reviewing function practical independence.
The review office can decide only whether the cutoff is authorized; it cannot impose 16:00 itself or operate the barrier for management.
If vehicles are to be banned at 16:00 as a general rule in the future, the manager can only submit that proposal to the body with authority to amend the rule.
mapping: The permit marked 17:00 → a general rule that exists before the day’s dispute.
The barrier lowered early → the executing body’s interpretation and action in response to sudden crowd conditions.
A review case that management cannot withdraw → an independent adjudicative function.
The 16:48 time stamp → the check directly changes whether Lin Su can enter at that moment.
The proposal for the following week → changing the general rule must return to the rule-making process.
module.boundary: Separation of powers does not guarantee that every decision is correct, and it does not mean that every matter requires agreement among multiple bodies. If formally separate functions are actually controlled through the same appointments, interests, or information, the constraint may be weak. Emergency procedures can move faster, but they should have a defined scope, records, a time limit, and review. The city, institutions, and event in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why is it important that the review office neither answers to plaza management nor has the power to create a 16:00 rule or personally operate the barrier?

moduleZh.intro: 一般规则先划定执行权的边界，执行机构再根据现场情况行动，独立裁决机构只判断解释是否越过授权。三种职能彼此制约，也各自保留完成本职工作的空间。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 规则、执行与裁决怎样在分立中彼此制约
diagramSteps: 一般规则先确定执行权的公开边界
执行机构面对现场情况采取具体行动
执行解释与既有规则发生争议
独立裁决机构只判断是否越过授权
若需改变一般规则，再回到规则制定环节
diagramStepNotes: 17:00时限先写在通行证上，管理处当天不能单凭自己的解释重写它。
管理处仍能缩窄通道、改单向和逐辆放行，说明分立没有取消执行能力。
复核工单不归管理处撤回或内部改判，体现裁决职能具有实际独立性。
复核室只能判断时限授权，不能自行规定16:00，也不能代替管理处操作栏杆。
以后若要普遍提前禁车，主管只能把建议提交有权修改一般规则的议事程序。
mapping: 写着17:00的通行证 → 先于当天争议存在的一般规则。
提前放下的栏杆 → 执行机构对突发人流作出的现场解释与行动。
不能被管理处撤回的复核工单 → 独立裁决职能。
16:48时间章 → 制约直接改变了林素当时能否进入。
下周禁车建议 → 改变一般规则必须回到规则制定环节。
moduleZh.boundary: 权力分立不保证每个决定都正确，也不等于任何事项都要多个机关一致。形式上的三套职能若受同一人事、利益或信息控制，制约可能很弱。紧急程序可以更快，但应有明确范围、记录、期限和复核。本故事中的城市、机构与活动均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么复核室既不能听命于管理处，又不能自己改成16:00或亲自指挥栏杆，反而是这项制约发挥作用的关键？

articles.title: The Orange Permit on Wednesday Morning
articles.titleZh: 星期三清晨的橙色许可
articles.summary: Every Wednesday from 06:00 to 08:00, Liu Sen’s street must be cleared for a street sweeper. The old notice cites an ordinance and the street really does become cleaner, yet Mara must push an elderly dialysis patient two extra blocks each week. At month’s end, a new notice keeps the same two hours.
articles.summaryZh: 每周三06:00–08:00，刘森所在的居民街都要腾空给清扫车。旧通知有条例依据，街道也确实更干净；玛拉却因此每周要推着透析老人多走两条街。月底，新通知仍写着同样的两个小时。
storyParagraphs: On Tuesday evening, Liu Sen came home to find a notice tucked under his windshield wiper: the entire street would be no-parking on Wednesday from 06:00 to 08:00, and vehicles left in place could be towed. The notice cited a sanitation ordinance allowing “temporary operational measures when necessary.” The next morning, most residents complied, the street sweeper passed through without difficulty, several weeks of leaves and broken glass were cleared away, and after 08:00 the cars gradually returned.

Mara, a care worker next door, began leaving forty minutes earlier from the second week onward. Every Wednesday at 06:30, she had to pick up an elderly person with limited mobility for dialysis. Normally she needed only ten minutes at the front door. Under the parking ban, she left her car two blocks away, walked back alone, and pushed the wheelchair to it. The sanitation staff did not single her out or deny that this was a burden; they only said the notice had an ordinance behind it, applied equally to all vehicles, and that 06:00 to 08:00 was the smoothest time for cleaning.

On the third Tuesday, Liu Sen went with Mara to the municipal service desk. The staff could still point to the same authorizing provision and confirm that the sanitation office had power to use temporary operational measures. But the old notice did not explain why the whole street had to be covered, why these two hours were fixed, how long the measure would continue, or who should handle Mara’s care-related need. The next morning, residents moved their cars as usual and the street was cleaned on time again. The fact that people complied did not answer those questions.

At the end of the month, a new notice appeared under Liu Sen’s wiper. The front still said 06:00–08:00, but the back now gave an end date for an eight-week trial, explained the turning space the sweeper required and why a later time was not being used, and listed how to apply for short care stops, disability transport, and emergency repairs. If an application was denied, a separate parking review office would handle the dispute. Mara submitted her care schedule and received an orange permit allowing a brief stop at the front door from 06:20 to 06:40.

On the next Wednesday, Liu Sen still moved his car to the nearby parking lot at 05:50; the two-hour burden had not disappeared. At 06:25, Mara placed the orange permit inside her windshield and helped the elderly patient into the car. The street sweeper waited for a few minutes at the previous intersection, then went around her position and continued. She did not have to ask the sweeper driver for a personal favor, and the permit did not exempt her from the rest of the Wednesday rules. After 08:00, the street was just as clean and the cars gradually returned as before.

When Liu Sen got home, he placed the old notice and the new eight-week trial notice in the same clear sleeve. Both fronts said “06:00–08:00.” The newer one had a review number and a clear end date in the lower-right corner, with the orange permit tucked between the two sheets.
storyParagraphsZh: 星期二傍晚，刘森回家时发现挡风玻璃下压着一张通知：周三06:00–08:00整条街禁止停车，未移车辆可被拖走。通知引用清洁条例里“必要时采取临时作业措施”的条款。第二天大多数住户都照做了，清扫车顺利通过，几周积下的落叶和碎玻璃一次清走，八点后车辆又陆续开回来。
隔壁照护员玛拉却从第二个星期开始提前四十分钟出门。她每周三六点半要接一位行动不便的老人去透析，原本只需在门口停十分钟。禁停后，她把车停到两条街外，再空手走回来推轮椅过去。清洁处的人没有针对她，也没有否认这项负担，只说通知有条例依据、对所有车辆一样，而且六点到八点清扫确实最顺。
第三个星期二，刘森陪玛拉去了市政服务台。工作人员仍能指出同一条授权条款，也确认清洁处有权采取临时作业措施，但旧通知没有说明为何必须整条街、为何固定这两个小时、措施会持续到什么时候，也没有告诉玛拉照护需要应由谁处理。第二天居民仍照常挪车，清扫仍按时完成；大家是否实际服从，并没有替这些问题作答。
月底，新的通知再次夹在刘森雨刷下。正面仍是06:00–08:00，背面多了八周试行的结束日期、清扫车所需转弯空间和选择这个时段的理由，并写明短时照护、残障接送和紧急维修的申请方式；若申请被拒，争议由另一个停车复核窗口处理。玛拉提交照护排班后，拿到一张橙色许可：06:20–06:40可以在门口短暂停靠。
新的星期三，刘森仍在五点五十分把车开去旁边停车场，两小时负担一点没消失。六点二十五分，玛拉把橙色许可放到挡风玻璃内侧，扶老人上车；清扫车在前一个路口等了几分钟，再绕过她的位置继续。她不需要向清扫司机临时求情，也没有因为拿到许可就免于其他周三规则。八点以后，街面同样干净，车辆也同样陆续开回。
刘森回家时，把旧通知和新的八周试行单夹进同一个透明袋。两张纸正面都写着“06:00–08:00”；后一张右下角多了一个复核编号和明确结束日期，橙色许可夹在中间。
explanationParagraphs: Political legitimacy asks why public power is entitled to make binding demands. Actual compliance, effective control, good outcomes, or formal legal authorization do not automatically answer that normative question.

Public reasons, limits, time boundaries, rights protection, and opportunities to challenge power may all contribute to justification, but no single indicator is necessarily sufficient, and legitimacy is not the same as popularity or majority approval.
explanationParagraphsZh: 政治合法性追问公共权力为何有资格提出有约束力的要求。事实服从、有效控制、好结果或形式法律依据，都不能自动回答这一规范问题。
公共理由、边界、期限、权利保护与可质疑性可能参与正当化，但没有一个单一指标必然充分，合法性也不等同于受欢迎或多数同意。
articles.overall: The old arrangement already has actual compliance, successful street cleaning, and an ordinance behind it, so the issue is not simply whether there is power or a legal provision. What changes under the eight-week arrangement is that the order explains why it operates this way, when it ends, how special burdens enter rights protection, and who reviews disputes. Both versions can control the street and achieve the cleaning goal, yet the claims they make on residents’ obedience do not therefore have exactly the same normative structure. The story does not treat the orange permit, a vote, or any single procedure as a sufficient formula for legitimacy.
articles.overallZh: 旧安排已经具备实际服从、清扫效果和条例依据，因此问题不是“有没有权力”或“有没有法律条文”。变化在于新的八周安排说明为何如此、到何时结束、特殊负担怎样进入权利保护，以及争议由谁复核。两版都能控制街道并完成清扫，但对居民提出的服从主张并不因此具有完全相同的规范结构；故事也不把橙色许可、表决或某一程序写成合法性的单一充分条件。

module.intro: Compliance, effective results, and legal authorization do not automatically explain why public power is entitled to demand obedience. Reasons, limits, duration, rights protection, and channels for review all shape how that claim to authority can be justified.
module.diagramTitle: How political legitimacy differs from actual compliance and effective control
diagramSteps: A public institution issues a binding order that it can actually enforce
Residents comply and the policy produces a real result
Formal authorization still leaves questions about reasons, limits, and rights
Time limits, rights protection, and review change the relationship between power and those subject to it
Continue distinguishing factual acceptance from normative justification
diagramStepNotes: The old notice has an ordinance behind it, residents comply, and the street becomes cleaner, so the story does not depend on a simple lack-of-authority problem.
Mara’s dialysis transport turns an abstract general rule into a concrete issue of burden and rights, rather than merely a question of clearer wording.
The new notice explains the timing and gives the trial an eight-week limit, making the scope and boundary of the power claim more explicit.
The orange permit and separate review process allow special burdens to enter rights protection, but neither one by itself guarantees legitimacy.
The 06:00–08:00 restriction and the cleaning outcome remain the same, showing that actual compliance and policy effectiveness cannot automatically equal normative justification.
mapping: Residents move their cars under both versions → descriptive compliance.
Both versions leave the street clean → effective results.
The old notice cites an ordinance → formal legal authorization is not a complete answer by itself.
The eight-week limit, stated reasons, care permit, and review channel → boundaries, rights protection, and contestability within the structure of justification.
Two notices both marked 06:00–08:00 → the same burden can accompany different kinds of claims to authority.
module.boundary: Political legitimacy is not the same as policy effectiveness, popularity, majority approval, the absence of coercion, or simple conformity with existing law. Different theories give different weight to consent, procedure, public reasons, rights, and democratic arrangements. The city, orders, and characters in this story are fictional.
module.reflection: Why do residents’ compliance, a cleaner street, and an ordinance behind the old notice still fail, by themselves, to answer why public authority is entitled to require obedience?

moduleZh.intro: 人们事实上服从、政策产生效果、命令也有法律依据，仍未自动回答公共权力为何有资格要求服从。理由、边界、期限、权利保护与复核渠道共同影响这项权力主张如何获得正当化。

diagramSteps: 公共机构提出能够实际执行的约束性命令

期限、权利保护和复核改变权力关系
继续区分事实接受与规范上的正当化
diagramStepNotes: 旧通知有条例依据、居民照做、街道变干净，因此故事不靠“无权乱收费式”问题成立。
玛拉的透析接送让一般命令的具体负担进入事件，而不是只讨论通知写得清不清楚。
新通知说明时段理由和八周期限，使权力主张出现可说明的范围与边界。
橙色许可和独立复核让特殊负担可以进入权利保护，但它们并不单独保证合法性。
06:00–08:00和清扫结果都没变，说明实际服从与政策有效性不能自动等同于规范正当性。
mapping: 居民两版都挪车 → 描述性的事实服从。
两版都把街道扫干净 → 有效结果。
旧通知引用条例 → 形式法律依据本身不是完整答案。
八周期限、理由、照护许可和复核渠道 → 正当化结构中的边界、权利保护与可质疑性。
两张都写06:00–08:00的通知 → 相同负担可以伴随不同性质的权威主张。
moduleZh.boundary: 政治合法性不等于政策有效、受欢迎、获得多数票、没有强制，也不等于只要符合现行条文便已回答全部规范问题。不同理论会赋予同意、程序、公共理由、权利与民主安排不同权重。本故事中的城市、命令和人物均为虚构。

articles.title: The Recording She Kept Not Opening
articles.titleZh: 那段一直没点开的录音
articles.summary: For years, Mei Ruo has insisted on anonymous first-round auditions with the same scoring system for everyone. She recognizes 17 as a former student and advances him; ten minutes later, the final sheet gives 17 a score of 82 and 23 a score of 86. She adds two unpublished criteria beside 17, then keeps avoiding 23’s backup recording.
articles.summaryZh: 梅若多年坚持第一轮匿名试音、统一评分。她认出17号是旧学生，先把他写进下一轮；十分钟后，总分表显示17号82分、23号86分。她在17号旁补上两项从未公布的标准，却一直没点开23号的备用录音。
storyParagraphs: On Tuesday evening, the community choir had to finalize its solo candidates before 10:00. Mei Ruo had already spent two hours listening to anonymous recordings. For several seasons, she had written into the audition notice that the first round would use numbers only and the same five scoring categories for everyone, and she had previously refused requests to see names in advance. But when she heard candidate 17, she recognized the voice of her former student Qiao Ning. With only three weeks left before the performance, she thought about how well he knew her conducting cues and wrote 17 onto the next-round list.

Ten minutes later, the assistant handed her the completed score summary. Candidate 17 had 82 points; candidate 23 had 86, with higher scores in both intonation and breath control. Mei Ruo did not change the list. Instead, she added “stage familiarity, rehearsal efficiency” beside 17. Neither item was part of the five first-round criteria that had been published in advance. When the assistant asked what to do about 23, she said to prepare the notification template first.

At home, Mei Ruo opened the audition email folder and saw the message she had sent to the entire choir the previous month: “First round anonymous. Use the same score sheet. Names are opened only at callbacks.” She closed the message and switched to 17’s backup recording. Candidate 23 had also uploaded a second clip. Her cursor paused over the filename, but she did not open it. The next day, when someone asked why 23 had not advanced, she said only, “Overall fit is not just about the numbers,” and closed the laptop.

At rehearsal that afternoon, 17 sang through a passage. Qiao Ning really was quick to follow Mei Ruo’s gestures, but one high note still needed to be lowered. During the break, the assistant placed a tablet on the piano; 23’s backup clip still showed “unplayed.” Mei Ruo went back to editing the score, then returned halfway through. At the top of the page were her own words: “anonymous first round.” She did not delete the rule, and she did not remove 17 from the list.

At 9:00 that evening, she finally opened 23’s backup recording and dragged 17’s version of the same passage beside it to listen again. She did not declare her earlier choice invalid or pretend it had never happened. Instead, she changed what happened next: both 17 and 23 received the same message inviting them to an added thirty-second live callback on Thursday, singing the same passage, with another conductor who had not taken part in the first-round scoring listening as well. The callback slot, originally reserved for only one person, grew by twenty minutes.

Before the Thursday callback began, two score sheets lay on the piano, marked only 17 and 23. Mei Ruo drew a thin line through “stage familiarity” beside 17 and left a new scoring box empty next to it. She laid the pen horizontally between the two numbered sheets. Someone was already waiting outside the door.
storyParagraphsZh: 周二晚上，社区合唱团要在十点前确定独唱候选人。梅若已经连续听了两个小时匿名录音；过去几季，她都把“第一轮只看编号、统一按五项评分”写进招募说明，还曾拒绝过提前查看姓名的请求。可听到17号时，她认出了旧学生乔宁的声音。离演出只剩三周，她想到乔宁熟悉自己的手势，先把17写进下一轮名单。
十分钟后，助理才把汇总完成的总分表递过来。17号82分，23号86分，而且23号在音准和呼吸两项都更高。梅若没有改名单，而是在17号旁边新添“熟悉舞台、排练效率高”。这两项原本不在第一轮公布的五项评分里。助理问23号怎么办，她让对方先准备通知模板。
回家后，梅若打开报名邮箱，看见自己上月发给全团的说明：“第一轮匿名，按同一张表走，名字到回调才打开。”她把那封邮件关掉，转去听17号的备用录音。23号也上传了第二段，她的鼠标停在文件名上，却没有点开。第二天有人问23号为何没进下一轮，她只说“整体适配不只看数字”，随后把电脑合上。
下午排练时，17号试唱了一段。乔宁确实熟悉梅若的手势，进入速度很快，但一个高音仍需要降调。休息时，助理把平板放到钢琴上，23号备用片段仍显示“未播放”。梅若先去改谱，改到一半又回来；页面最上方还写着她自己的“匿名第一轮”。她没有删除那句规则，也没有把17号从名单上划掉。
晚上九点，她终于点开23号的备用录音，又把17号同一段拖到旁边重听。她没有宣布自己先前的选择无效，也没有把它包装成从未发生，而是改变了下一步：给17和23都发出同一条消息，周四增加一轮三十秒现场回调，唱同一段旋律，再请一名没参与前轮评分的指挥一起听。原本只给一个人的回调时段因此多占了二十分钟。
周四开始前，钢琴上放着两张只写编号的谱页：17和23。梅若把17号旁边那句“熟悉舞台”用细线划掉，旁边留着一个新的评分格。她把笔横放在两张谱页之间，门外已经有人在等。
explanationParagraphs: Cognitive dissonance is the discomfort that can arise when an action already taken conflicts with a valued commitment, evidence, or self-understanding. People may reduce the conflict by adding justifications, selectively approaching information, or changing what they do next.

It is not the same as every case of favoritism, hesitation, or rationalization, and it does not require the person to be completely innocent. The key is whether behavior after the conflict appears to move toward reducing the inconsistency.
explanationParagraphsZh: 认知失调指已作出的行动与珍视的承诺、证据或自我理解发生不一致后产生的不适。人可能通过增加理由、选择性接触信息或改变后续行动来减轻冲突。
它不等于任何偏袒、犹豫或合理化，也不要求当事人完全无辜；关键在于冲突出现后，行为是否朝减轻不一致的方向变化。
articles.overall: Mei Ruo advances 17 because she recognizes and favors him, and the story does not excuse that choice. What is specifically relevant to cognitive dissonance is what follows: only after the 82-versus-86 evidence appears does she add criteria that were not on the original score sheet and avoid 23’s recording. When those moves become harder to maintain, she reduces the conflict in another way by changing the next action and adding an equal callback. The story therefore distinguishes the earlier favoritism from how she deals with the self-conflict that follows it.
articles.overallZh: 梅若先因熟悉17号而让他晋级，这个选择本身带有偏袒成分，并没有被故事洗白。真正与认知失调相关的是随后发生的减压路径：82对86的证据出现后，她才补写不在原评分表里的理由、回避23号录音；当这些做法越来越难维持，她又通过同条件回调改变后续行动。故事因此把偏袒行为与偏袒之后如何处理自我冲突区分开。

module.intro: Mei Ruo has long defended a public standard of fairness, then makes a choice that conflicts with it. The later scores sharpen that conflict. She adds reasons, avoids information, and eventually changes her next action to deal with the inconsistency.
module.diagramTitle: How ways of reducing tension can change after a choice conflicts with a valued standard
diagramSteps: A person begins with a long-held and publicly maintained standard
They first make a choice that sits uneasily with that standard
Later evidence makes the inconsistency sharper
They reduce the conflict by adding reasons or avoiding information
They may also change the next action to deal with the conflict differently
diagramStepNotes: Anonymous first-round review and the same five scoring categories have been publicly used across several seasons, so the fairness standard is not invented after the fact.
Mei Ruo advances 17 before seeing the final summary showing 17 at 82 and 23 at 86.
“Stage familiarity, rehearsal efficiency” is added only after the score conflict appears, and neither item belonged to the original five first-round criteria.
Candidate 23’s backup recording remains unplayed, showing selective exposure to information rather than simple lack of access.
The equal callback changes the next action but does not erase Mei Ruo’s earlier favoritism toward 17 or turn the ending into moral absolution.
mapping: Long-standing public anonymous scoring → Mei Ruo’s genuinely valued fairness standard.
17 advances first, followed by the 82-versus-86 result → an existing choice comes into conflict with later evidence.
Adding “stage familiarity” → a new justification introduced after the conflict appears.
Not opening 23’s backup recording → selective contact with information after the conflict.
Two equally structured numbered callback sheets → another way of reducing the tension by changing the next action.
module.boundary: Cognitive dissonance does not excuse all favoritism, poor judgment, or deliberate cheating, and it is not an automatic diagnosis for every rationalization. The story presents only one possible path: after an earlier choice conflicts with a valued standard, the person manages the discomfort through reasons, information exposure, and later action. The characters, choir, and auditions are fictional.
module.reflection: Why does cognitive dissonance not explain away Mei Ruo’s initial favoritism toward 17, while the added justification, avoided recording, and new callback after the 82-versus-86 result are the changes the story is actually examining?

moduleZh.intro: 梅若长期公开维护一套公平标准，却先作出了与它有张力的选择。后来出现的分数让冲突变得尖锐，她增加理由、避开信息，最后又通过改变下一步行动来处理这种不一致。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 已作出的选择与自我标准冲突后，减压路径怎样变化
diagramSteps: 先存在长期珍视并公开坚持的标准
先作出与该标准有张力的选择
随后证据让不一致变得更尖锐
当事人通过加理由或避开信息减轻冲突
也可能改动后续行动以重新处理冲突
diagramStepNotes: 匿名第一轮和统一五项评分在多个季度公开使用，说明公平标准并非事后发明。
梅若先让17号晋级，之后才看到17号82分、23号86分的汇总表。
“熟悉舞台、排练效率高”是在分数冲突出现后新增，而且原本不属于第一轮五项标准。
23号备用录音停在未播放状态，体现选择性接触信息，而不是单纯信息缺失。
同条件回调改变的是后续行动，并不抹去她先前偏袒17号的选择，也不是道德洗白。
mapping: 长期公开的匿名统一评分 → 梅若真实珍视的公平标准。
17号先晋级、随后出现82对86 → 已作出的选择与证据发生冲突。
新增“熟悉舞台” → 冲突出现后的协调理由。
未点开的23号备用录音 → 冲突出现后的选择性信息接触。
17和23两张同条件谱页 → 另一种减压路径：改变下一步行动。
moduleZh.boundary: 认知失调不能替所有偏袒、能力不足或蓄意作弊开脱，也不是对任何合理化的自动诊断。故事只呈现一种可能路径：既有选择与珍视标准冲突后，当事人通过理由、信息接触和后续行动处理不适。人物、合唱团与试音均为虚构。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么梅若先偏向17号并不能由认知失调解释掉，而82对86出现之后的补理由、回避录音与新增回调才构成故事真正要观察的变化？

references.citation: Festinger, Leon. *A Theory of Cognitive Dissonance*. Stanford University Press, 1957.
references.use: Used to support the classic account that cognitive inconsistency can produce dissonance and that people may reduce it by changing cognitions, adding consonant cognitions, or reducing the importance of dissonant cognitions.

references.citation: Harmon-Jones, Eddie, and Judson Mills. “An Introduction to Cognitive Dissonance Theory and an Overview of Current Perspectives on the Theory.” In *Cognitive Dissonance: Reexamining a Pivotal Theory in Psychology*, 2nd ed., 3–24. American Psychological Association, 2019.
references.use: Used to support modern overviews of dissonance theory, the tension-reduction process following inconsistency between behavior and cognition, and boundaries involving self-concept, action tendencies, and alternative explanations.

referencesZh.citation: Festinger, Leon. *A Theory of Cognitive Dissonance*. Stanford University Press, 1957.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持认知不一致产生失调，以及人会通过改变认知、增加协调认知或降低不协调认知的重要性来减少失调的经典理论。

referencesZh.citation: Harmon-Jones, Eddie, and Judson Mills. “An Introduction to Cognitive Dissonance Theory and an Overview of Current Perspectives on the Theory.” In *Cognitive Dissonance: Reexamining a Pivotal Theory in Psychology*, 2nd ed., 3–24. American Psychological Association, 2019.
referencesZh.use: 用于支持失调理论的现代综述、行为与认知不一致后的减压过程，以及自我概念、行动倾向与替代理论边界。

articles.title: Ten Minutes Beside the Red Charging Rack
articles.summary: The morning crew finds two uncharged batteries again. Xiao Yu wants to try a purple rim light, with only the last ten minutes before the studio closes available.
storyParagraphs: On Monday morning, two batteries are once again lying at the bottom of the equipment cart instead of in the red charging rack. Lin Qiu, who runs the studio, checks the same closing sheet for the previous eight evening shifts. Under the existing rule, equipment must be put away, every used battery placed in the red rack, and the routine checks completed by 21:50; the studio locks at 22:00. Across those eight shifts, the battery item was completed on time only three times.

Xiao Yu has recently wanted to practice lighting with colored gels. When normal closing work is fully finished by 21:50, the studio already has ten minutes of slack before lockup; on most evenings, people simply wait for closing. Lin Qiu places an unused light and several gels on the worktable and makes an arrangement with him: if all batteries used that day are also in the rack by the same 21:50 deadline, he may use the remaining ten minutes for his own lighting tests.

That evening, Xiao Yu parks the equipment cart beside the charging cabinet first, matches the used batteries by number, and puts them in the red rack before folding the last backdrop. He stores the lenses and checks the cables, locks, and closing list as usual. At 21:49, every closing task is finished. Only then does he clip a blue gel onto the spare light and try two angles. At 21:59, he puts the gel away and switches off the test light. When he locks up at 22:00, his phone holds two new blue-violet photographs; the 22:17 metro is still his usual train.

Over the next several shifts, he starts wheeling the cart to the charging cabinet as soon as he unloads the camera, its strap still hanging from the handle. Once the batteries and other closing tasks are finished, he takes out a gel to try a color. One evening, the battery box on the list is not checked until 21:53; the gels stay in their bag. After lockup, Xiao Yu looks through photographs from earlier nights on the station platform and notes another angle he wants to try.

Two weeks later, Lin Qiu puts the two sets of closing sheets side by side: three on-time battery checkmarks in the earlier eight shifts, seven in the later eight. The one late sheet has “21:53” written beside it. The reminder sign is still beside the door. The cart’s parking place has changed, and a faint wheel mark now runs along the floor in front of the charging cabinet.

At the end of one evening shift later that month, Xiao Yu slides the last battery into the red rack, checks off the list, and looks up at the wall clock: 21:50. A purple gel lies on the worktable. He picks it up and walks toward the unused light.
articles.overall: Operant conditioning concerns how consequences change the future frequency of behavior. This example uses positive reinforcement: an opportunity for practice is added after the target behavior, and that behavior later becomes more frequent. “Positive” means addition; reinforcement is judged by the change in behavior.
explanationParagraphs: Across the eight evening shifts before the arrangement, all used batteries were in the rack by 21:50 on three occasions; across the next eight, this happened seven times. The extra lighting opportunity becomes available only after the target behavior is completed on time, while the existing checks, closing time, and commute remain unchanged.

Positive reinforcement requires an added consequence after behavior and greater frequency later. Liking a reward alone is insufficient. These before-and-after records may also be affected by reminders, interest, relationships, and other changes, so they are not a controlled causal experiment.

module.intro: Positive reinforcement requires the same target behavior, the same criterion, an added consequence after the behavior, and a later increase in the behavior’s frequency.
module.diagramTitle: From 3/8 to 7/8 Under the Same 21:50 Deadline
diagramSteps: Record the original frequency of the same target behavior across eight shifts
Place the lighting opportunity after completion of the target behavior
Keep existing checks and closing time unchanged
Observe whether Xiao Yu changes his closing sequence on his own
Compare the next eight shifts using the same deadline
diagramStepNotes: The target is to have all batteries used that day in the red rack by 21:50; originally this occurred in 3 of 8 shifts.
After batteries and other closing tasks are finished, up to ten minutes before lockup are available for practice; the light is switched off and put away afterward.
The studio still locks at 22:00 and the 22:17 metro remains unchanged.
Xiao Yu begins pushing the equipment cart to the charging cabinet first.
Across the next 8 shifts, the same standard is met 7 times.
mapping: Red charging rack → the observable endpoint of the target behavior.
21:50 deadline → the common criterion used in the before-and-after comparison.
Ten minutes of gel-lighting practice → the added consequence after the behavior.
3/8 to 7/8 → change in the later frequency of the behavior.
module.boundary: In positive reinforcement, “positive” means adding a consequence, not moral goodness, and “reinforcement” is judged by whether the behavior becomes more frequent in the future. This fictional story illustrates the mechanism but cannot strictly establish a single cause, because reminders, interest, relationships, and other uncontrolled factors may also affect behavior.
module.reflection: If the before and after periods used different completion standards or deadlines, why would a higher number alone be insufficient to show that the target behavior truly became more frequent?

references.citation: Skinner, B. F. (1938). The Behavior of Organisms: An Experimental Analysis. Appleton-Century.
references.use: Supports an early systematic treatment of operant conditioning; it is not used to claim that Skinner invented all theories of learning.

references.citation: OpenStax (2020). Psychology 2e, §6.3: Operant Conditioning.
references.use: Supports defining reinforcement by an increase in future behavior frequency, and positive/negative as adding or removing a stimulus rather than good or bad.

articles.summaryZh: 两块没充电的电池又被早班翻了出来。小俞想试一组紫色边光，摄影棚却只剩关门前的十分钟。
storyParagraphsZh: 周一早上，摄影棚开机前又有两块电池躺在器材车底层，没进红色充电槽。负责人林秋翻了过去八个晚班的同一张收班表：按原规定，二十一点五十分前要完成器材归位、用过的电池全部入红槽和例行检查，之后二十二点锁门。八个晚班里，电池这一项只有三次按时完成。
小俞最近想练彩色凝胶布光。正常收班若在二十一点五十分前全部完成，原本就会留出十分钟机动时间；大多数晚上大家只是等到锁门。林秋把一盏空闲灯和几片凝胶放到工作台旁，和小俞约定：只要当天用过的电池也在同一截止点前全部入槽，这十分钟就可以拿来做自己的灯光测试。
当晚，小俞先把器材车停到充电柜旁，按编号把用过的电池放进红槽，再去折最后一块背景布。他照常归好镜头，核对线缆、门锁和清单。二十一点四十九分，收班项目全部完成，他才把蓝色凝胶夹到空闲灯前，试了两个角度。二十一点五十九分，他收好胶片，关掉试灯电源；二十二点锁门时，手机里已经多了两张蓝紫色照片，二十二点十七分的地铁照旧。
接下来几次晚班，他卸完相机就先把车推到充电柜，背带还挂在扶手上。电池归好、其他收班项目结束，他便取一片凝胶试颜色。有一晚清单齐了，电池那一栏却到了二十一点五十三分才勾上，凝胶片仍留在袋里。锁门以后，小俞在站台翻着前几晚的照片，把想试的另一种角度记进手机。
两周后，林秋把前后两叠收班表并排放着：原来的八班有三个按时完成归槽的勾，后来的八班有七个。唯一没赶上那一张，旁边记着二十一点五十三分。门边提醒牌还贴在原处；器材车停靠的位置变了，充电柜前的地面上多出一道浅浅的轮印。
月底一个晚班结束，小俞把最后一块电池插进红槽，勾完清单，抬头看了眼墙钟：二十一点五十。工作台上压着一片紫色凝胶，他拿起它走向那盏空闲灯。
articles.overallZh: 操作性条件作用关注行为后果如何改变以后同类行为的频率。这里采用正强化：目标行为之后增加一个可获得的练习机会，随后行为更常出现；“正”表示增加，“强化”看实际变化。
explanationParagraphsZh: 安排前八个晚班中，二十一点五十分前完整归槽三次；安排后八个晚班中七次完成。额外试灯机会只在目标行为按时完成后可用，且原有检查、关棚和通勤时间不变。
正强化的判断依据是行为后增加结果、以后行为更常发生。喜欢某项奖励本身不足以成立；这组前后记录仍可能受提醒、兴趣、人际关系及其他变化影响，不能当成受控因果实验。

moduleZh.intro: 正强化要看同一目标行为、同一判定标准、行为后的新增结果，以及之后频率是否上升。
diagramSteps: 记录原有八个晚班的同一目标频率
把试灯机会放在目标行为完成之后
保持原有检查与锁门时间不变
观察小俞是否主动改变收班顺序
用同一截止点比较后续八个晚班
diagramStepNotes: 目标是21:50前把当天用过的电池全部入红槽；原来8班完成3次。
电池和其他收班项目完成后，关棚前最多十分钟可用于试灯；用完须关灯归位。
小俞开始先把器材车推到充电柜。
后续8班按同一标准完成7次。
mapping: 红色充电槽 → 目标行为的可观察终点。
21:50截止点 → 前后比较保持一致的判定标准。
十分钟凝胶试灯 → 行为完成后增加的结果。
3/8到7/8 → 后续行为频率变化。
moduleZh.boundary: 正强化中的“正”指增加结果，不表示好坏；“强化”要由未来行为频率是否增加来判断。这个虚构故事展示机制，不足以严格证明单一因果，因为提醒、兴趣、人际关系和其他未控制因素也可能影响行为。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果前后使用不同的完成标准或截止时间，为什么即使数字变高，也不能直接说目标行为频率真的增加了？

referencesZh.citation: Skinner, B. F. (1938). The Behavior of Organisms: An Experimental Analysis. Appleton-Century.
referencesZh.use: 支持操作性条件作用的早期系统论述；不把Skinner写成凭空发明全部学习理论。

referencesZh.citation: OpenStax (2020). Psychology 2e, §6.3: Operant Conditioning.
referencesZh.use: 支持强化以未来行为频率增加来定义，以及正/负分别指增加或移除刺激而非好坏。

articles.title: The Old Textbook That Stalled at Counter A
articles.summary: Counter A’s queue reaches the engineering shelves, and Jianing has been listed for speed training. At lunchtime, another colleague takes her place.
storyParagraphs: During textbook exchange week, just before classes begin, Counter A’s queue bends around the engineering shelves. Students wait with stacks of old books in their arms. Between restocking jobs, supervisor Zhou Ke checks the transaction summary: A takes one or two minutes longer per exchange than B. Jianing usually works at A, but Zhou Ke has only caught glimpses of the queue and has not watched a complete transaction. Beside the rota, she writes, “Jianing: speed training next week,” to arrange after the exchange rush.

Before lunch on Wednesday, the employee at Counter B is called to the stockroom to receive a shipment of new books, so Jianing covers B for twenty minutes. That counter mostly receives newer editions and has an updated scanner. She processes six transactions in a row at roughly the same speed as ordinary exchanges handled by the rest of the team. When the other employee returns, Jianing goes back to Counter A, and the queue slows again.

This time Zhou Ke is standing nearby. A student places three older engineering textbooks on the counter. The barcode on one 2019 edition is worn, and Counter A’s old scanner cannot read it. Jianing has to open the copyright page, type the ISBN manually, and then wait for the shared printer to produce a replacement label. Zhou Ke then notices that the sign at the entrance has always said, “Older editions and books without barcodes: Counter A.”

When Jianing goes to lunch, senior colleague A-Mo takes over at A. Before long, he gets an old textbook that will not scan, opens the copyright page, types its ISBN, and waits for the same printer. Zhou Ke opens the detailed transaction log and marks the older editions and books without barcodes: most have gone to A. She then finds Jianing’s exchanges of newer books at A; their times fall within the range of her colleagues’ ordinary exchanges. In front of A-Mo, the next student has already opened a book at its copyright page.

That afternoon, Zhou Ke puts the newer spare scanner at A and moves the old-edition routing sign between the counters. She asks waiting students to use whichever side has space, separating the queue crowded beside the shelves. Over the afternoon, A’s average time for ordinary exchanges falls and the gap between Jianing and her colleagues narrows. The shared printer remains on its original table; both counters still wait for replacement labels. Zhou Ke adds that item to the equipment list.

Over the weekend, Jianing encounters a complicated refund involving a revised-edition textbook and a payment method that does not match the original purchase. She is still unfamiliar with that refund sequence, so she stops to check the procedure sheet and asks A-Mo to confirm it. Zhou Ke changes the rota note to “practice complex refund procedure once more.” The final student places an older textbook on Counter A; the new scanner reads the barcode on the first try, and Jianing prints the label and pushes the book into the returns cart.
articles.overall: The fundamental attribution error is a tendency to give too much weight to character or ability and too little to circumstances when explaining another person’s behavior. Comparing the same person across settings and different people in similar settings can revise that judgment; individual differences still need specific examination.
explanationParagraphs: Zhou Ke initially has only average transaction times and queue length, so “Jianing is slow” is reasonable but incomplete. Jianing’s shift to Counter B, A-Mo’s ordinary takeover of A, and the differences in old books and scanner conditions add comparable situational evidence.

Because the routing sign and scanner change at the same time, their separate effects cannot be identified. Jianing still has a specific skill gap in complex refunds, so revising the situational attribution does not erase all individual differences.

module.intro: Break poor performance into specific tasks, then use comparable information about people and settings to revise each part of the judgment.
module.diagramTitle: From Backend Timing Data to Seeing the Process at Counter A
diagramSteps: Form an initial personal explanation from aggregate transaction times
Let the same person move to another counter through ordinary staffing needs
Directly observe task and tool constraints at Counter A
Use a natural handover to obtain another person’s comparable performance
After contextual changes, narrow the remaining training need
diagramStepNotes: Counter A is consistently slower, while Zhou Ke has not yet watched a full transaction.
Jianing covers Counter B for six transactions and handles ordinary exchanges at roughly peer speed.
Older books concentrate at A, and the old scanner often requires manual ISBN entry.
A-Mo covers A at lunch and is slowed by the same steps.
Ordinary exchanges improve after the environment changes, while complex refunds still reveal a specific unfamiliar step.
mapping: Backend average time → basis for the initial attribution under limited information.
Worn old barcode and shared printer → visible situational constraints.
Covering Counter B and A-Mo taking over A → two naturally occurring comparisons.
Refund procedure sheet → a specific individual skill that still needs practice.
module.boundary: Situational evidence can weaken an overly strong personal attribution, but it cannot prove that ability or character never matters or excuse every error. Because the scanner and routing change together, the story cannot estimate their separate effects; culture and information conditions also influence attribution tendencies.
module.reflection: If you initially had only average transaction times, but later saw the same person in another setting and another person in the original setting, how would you revise your first judgment about individual ability?

references.citation: Ross, L. (1977). The Intuitive Psychologist and His Shortcomings: Distortions in the Attribution Process. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 10, 173–220.
references.use: Supports the classic theoretical account of over-weighting personal factors and under-weighting situational factors in attribution; the fictional story is not presented as a replication of a real experiment.

references.citation: OpenStax (2020). Psychology 2e, §12.1: What Is Social Psychology?
references.use: Supports the teaching definition of the fundamental attribution error, situational constraints, and cultural boundaries while preserving the possibility that dispositional explanations can sometimes have support.

articles.titleZh: 那本旧版教材卡在A柜台
articles.summaryZh: A柜台的长队拐到了工程书架，佳宁又被记下需要速度训练。那天中午，另一位同事来接她的班。
storyParagraphsZh: 开学前的教材交换周，书店A柜台的队伍弯到工程书架旁，等候的学生抱着一摞摞旧教材。主管周珂在补库存的间隙看后台汇总：A柜台平均每单比B柜台多一两分钟。佳宁大多守A，周珂这几天只零碎看过长队，还没从头跟完一单。她在排班表旁写下“佳宁：下周补速度训练”，准备等交换周结束再安排。
周三午前，B柜台同事被叫去后仓接一车新书，佳宁临时过去顶二十分钟。B柜台主要收新版教材，扫码枪也更新。她连续处理六单，耗时接近同组其他人的普通换书单。等同事回来，佳宁回A柜台，队伍又慢下来。
这一次周珂刚好站在旁边，看见一个学生推来三本旧版工程教材。其中一本2019年的条码磨花，A柜台的旧扫码枪读不出，佳宁只好翻版权页手输ISBN，再等共享打印机吐出新标签。周珂随后注意到门口分流牌一直写着“旧版及无条码教材请到A柜台”。
午饭时佳宁离开，资深同事阿莫接手A柜台。没多久，他也碰到一册扫不出的旧教材，翻版权页手输ISBN，等同一台打印机。周珂打开当天明细，把旧版和无条码书标出来：这些书大多到了A柜台。她又找出佳宁在A处理新版书的几笔记录，耗时落在同事普通换书单的范围里。阿莫面前，下一位学生已经把书翻到版权页等着了。
下午，周珂给A换上备用的新扫码枪，把旧版教材分流牌移到两个柜台之间。她请排队的人按两边空位走，把原来挤在书架旁的队伍分开。后半天的普通换书单里，A的平均耗时降了，佳宁和同事的差距也小了。共享打印机还在原来的桌上，两边需要补标签时仍会等纸，周珂将这一项另记在设备清单上。
周末，佳宁遇到一笔复杂退款：她对“已换版教材＋原付款方式不一致”的退款步骤还不熟，停下来查流程表并请阿莫确认。周珂把排班表上的备注改成“复杂退款流程再练一次”。最后一位学生把旧版教材放上A柜台，新扫码枪一次读出条码，佳宁打印标签后把书推入回收车。
articles.overallZh: 基本归因错误是解释他人行为时，过多看重性格或能力、过少考虑情境约束的倾向。比较同一个人在不同条件下、不同人在相似条件下的表现，有助于修正判断；个人差异仍需具体核查。
explanationParagraphsZh: 周珂最初只有汇总耗时和长队信息，因此“佳宁慢”是合理但不充分的解释。佳宁换到B柜台、阿莫自然接A柜台，以及旧版书和扫码工具差异，增加了可比情境证据。
分流牌和扫码枪同时调整后，无法单独识别各自效应；复杂退款中佳宁仍有具体技能缺口。情境修正不等于否认所有个人差异。

moduleZh.intro: 先把“表现差”拆成具体任务，再找人与情境的可比信息，逐项修正判断。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从后台耗时到看清A柜台过程
diagramSteps: 用汇总耗时形成初步个人解释
因普通排班让同一个人换到另一柜台
直接看到A柜台的任务与工具约束
由自然接班获得其他人的可比表现
调整情境后重新缩小个人训练问题
diagramStepNotes: A柜台长期更慢，周珂尚未完整观察单笔流程。
佳宁临时顶B柜台六单，普通单耗时接近同事。
旧版书集中A柜台，旧扫码枪常需手输ISBN。
阿莫午饭接A柜台，也被相同步骤拖慢。
环境调整后普通单改善，复杂退款仍有具体不熟步骤。
mapping: 后台平均耗时 → 信息不足时的初步归因依据。
磨花旧条码与共享打印机 → 可见情境约束。
B柜台顶班与阿莫接A → 两种自然可比信息。
退款流程表 → 仍需训练的具体个人技能。
moduleZh.boundary: 情境证据可以削弱过强的个人归因，但不能证明个人能力完全无关，也不能为所有失误免责。扫码枪和分流同时改变，因此故事不能单独估计各自效果；文化与信息条件也会影响归因倾向。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果你最初只有平均耗时，却后来看到同一个人换情境和其他人进入原情境的表现，你会怎样修改原先的个人能力判断？

referencesZh.use: 支持归因过程中高估个人因素、低估情境因素的经典理论论述；不把虚构故事写成真实实验复现。
